135	                 [--resume] [--from-stage <stage>] [--no-resume] [--force]
136	  --issue <N>       GitHub issue number to work
137	  --goal "<text>"   Pipeline goal description (alternative to --issue)
138	  --dry-run         Print the stage plan without executing anything
139	  --template <id>   Pipeline template to use (default: simple)
140	  --resume          Resume an existing run (skip completed stages)
141	  --from-stage <s>  Skip ahead to stage <s> when resuming (emits warning)
142	  --no-resume       Recreate: start fresh even if a state exists and restore no
143	                    prior-run work (default: resume, reusing prior work;
144	                    ZBUILD_RESUME=0 is the same, #2225)
145	  --force           Resume even if status=aborted
146	  --self-host       Dogfood zBuild's own engine: redirect read-only contract-
147	                    grammar libs to a working-tree snapshot (#963, ADR-023)
148	
149	Environment:
150	  ZBUILD_PLATFORM_OVERRIDE  Force a single platform; detection short-circuits.
151	  ZBUILD_SCOPE_PATHS        Newline-delimited scope paths; written as '+ <path>' entries.
152	  ZBUILD_SELF_HOST          Set to 1 to enable self-host mode (same as --self-host).
153	  ZBUILD_CONTRACT_LIB_DIR   Override dir contract-reader stages source grammar libs from.
154	EOF

157	# Helpers extracted to dispatch.sh / state_helpers.sh in #279:
158	#   _find_plugin_for_stage       → core/pipeline/dispatch.sh
159	#   write_scope_override
160	#   _update_stage_status         } → core/pipeline/state_helpers.sh
161	#   _set_pipeline_status
162	#   (+ their _zbuild_runner_set_* jq filter helpers)
163	
164	# Globals (not local) so EXIT trap can read them after main() returns.
165	_runner_run_id="" _runner_issue="" _runner_ended=false _runner_state_file=""
166	# ADR-054 §11 (#1944): run-level watchdog globals — PID of the watchdog background
167	# subshell (killed by the EXIT trap on clean exit) and the resolved limit in seconds.
168	_RUNNER_WATCHDOG_PID=""
169	_RUNNER_MAX_RUN_S=""
170	# #1878: last reported snapshot-failure reason, so a static precondition is
171	# reported once rather than once per stage boundary.
172	_RUNNER_LAST_SNAPSHOT_FAIL_REASON=""

174	# ─── _runner_leaf_contract_halt <state_file> <stage> <reason> ───────────────
175	# A leaf stage whose v2 result the engine rejected ends the run; rc 0 when it
176	# did. A cycle already halts on this (#550); a leaf recorded `error` and went on,
177	# which is how #1835's run shipped a plan result with no `reason`. Safe ahead of
178	# #1798: a contract violation is a zBuild defect (ADR-054 §6 `broken`), never a
179	# transient failure, so this cannot turn a network hiccup into a dead run.
180	# Reads main()'s _runner_run_id / _runner_issue and sets its _runner_ended.
181	_runner_leaf_contract_halt() {
182	    local sf="$1" st="$2" why="${3:-}"
183	    [[ "$why" == contract_violation:* ]] || return 1
184	    _update_stage_status "$sf" "$st" "failed"
185	    _set_pipeline_status "$sf" "failed"
186	    eb_emit_event "stage.fail" "stage=$st" "reason=$why" 2>/dev/null || true
187	    eb_emit_event "pipeline.end" "status=failed" "stage=$st" "reason=$why" \
188	        "run_id=${_runner_run_id:-}" "issue=${_runner_issue:-}" 2>/dev/null || true
189	    _render_pipeline_end "failed" "$st"
190	    _runner_ended=true
191	    error "Stage $st wrote a result the engine rejects ($why) — a zBuild defect; the run stops here"
192	    return 0
193	}
194	
195	# ─── _runner_leaf_verdict_halt <state_file> <stage> <class> <raw> ────────────
196	# #1798 (ADR-054 §4): a leaf stage that reports a failure ends the run; rc 0
197	# when it did. <class> is the classified verdict the runner already read
198	# (runner_read_stage_verdict: fail, or a structural word passed through);
199	# <raw> is the stage's own word, which the run's end names. A cycle acts on its
200	# members' verdicts; a leaf used to record one, pick a glyph from it and
201	# complete anyway. A template opts a stage out with `blocking: false`
202	# (ADR-013) — advisory by declaration, never by accident.
203	_runner_leaf_verdict_halt() {
204	    local sf="$1" st="$2" v="${3:-}" raw="${4:-}"
205	    case "$v" in
206	        fail|error|block|scope_violation|corrupt_diff) ;;
207	        *) return 1 ;;
208	    esac
209	    [[ "$(template_stage_blocking "$st" 2>/dev/null)" == "false" ]] && return 1
210	    [[ -n "$raw" && "$raw" != "missing" ]] || raw="$v"
211	    _update_stage_status "$sf" "$st" "failed"
212	    _zbuild_state_set_stage_verdict "$sf" "$st" "$v"
213	    _set_pipeline_status "$sf" "failed"
214	    # No `rc=` field: the stage exited 0, so a verdict-triggered stage.fail
215	    # carries the stage's word (`verdict=`) instead — as the contract halt
216	    # carries `reason=` alone. A consumer of stage.fail reads either shape.
217	    eb_emit_event "stage.fail" "stage=$st" "verdict=$raw" "reason=stage_failed:$raw" 2>/dev/null || true
218	    eb_emit_event "pipeline.end" "status=failed" "stage=$st" "reason=stage_failed:$raw" \
219	        "run_id=${_runner_run_id:-}" "issue=${_runner_issue:-}" 2>/dev/null || true
220	    _render_pipeline_end "failed" "$st"
221	    _runner_ended=true
222	    error "Stage $st reported $raw — the run stops here"
223	    return 0
224	}

226	# ─── _runner_note_push_failure <stage> (#2187) ───────────────────────────────
227	# Report a failed stage-end push once per distinct reason, on the same channel
228	# and dedupe as a failed snapshot.
229	_runner_note_push_failure() {
230	    [[ "${_ARTIFACT_PERSIST_LAST_STATUS:-}" == "failed" ]] || return 0
231	    [[ "${_ARTIFACT_PERSIST_LAST_REASON:-}" != "${_RUNNER_LAST_SNAPSHOT_FAIL_REASON:-}" ]] || return 0
232	    _RUNNER_LAST_SNAPSHOT_FAIL_REASON="${_ARTIFACT_PERSIST_LAST_REASON:-unknown}"
233	    eb_emit_event "artifact.snapshot.failed" "stage=${1:-unknown}" "issue=$_runner_issue" \
234	        "reason=${_ARTIFACT_PERSIST_LAST_REASON:-unknown}" 2>/dev/null || true
235	    warn "stage-end push failed at stage '${1:-unknown}': ${_ARTIFACT_PERSIST_LAST_REASON:-unknown}"
236	}
237	
238	# ─── _runner_push_work_branch <state_dir> <stage> (#2187) ────────────────────
239	# When the run has a work branch on origin (ZBUILD_WORKSPACE_BRANCH — CI sets
240	# zbuild/issue-N-ci), push the run's commits to it at every stage end, so a new
241	# session can pick them up even if this runner dies. No changes, no save: only
242	# when HEAD carries commits past the commit the run started from, which the
243	# engine sets before any stage (#2367; #1801 run 38290215955: the end of hydrate
244	# force-pushed main over the branch's earlier work). Advisory: a failure is
245	# reported, never fatal.
246	_runner_push_work_branch() {
247	    local _branch="${ZBUILD_WORKSPACE_BRANCH:-}"
248	    [[ -n "$_branch" ]] || return 0
249	    local _repo="${ZBUILD_REPO_ROOT:-}"
250	    [[ -n "$_repo" ]] || _repo="$(git rev-parse --show-toplevel 2>/dev/null || true)"
251	    [[ -n "$_repo" ]] || return 0
252	    git -C "$_repo" remote get-url origin >/dev/null 2>&1 || return 0
253	    local _base="${ZBUILD_RUN_START_COMMIT:-}" _ahead
254	    [[ -n "$_base" ]] || return 0
255	    _ahead="$(git -C "$_repo" rev-list --count "$_base..HEAD" 2>/dev/null || echo 0)"
256	    [[ "$_ahead" =~ ^[0-9]+$ && "$_ahead" -gt 0 ]] || return 0
257	    local _err
258	    if _err="$(git -C "$_repo" push --force -q origin "HEAD:refs/heads/$_branch" 2>&1)"; then
259	        return 0
260	    fi
261	    _ARTIFACT_PERSIST_LAST_STATUS="failed"
262	    _ARTIFACT_PERSIST_LAST_REASON="git push work branch $_branch failed: $(tr '\n' ' ' <<< "$_err" | cut -c1-300)"
263	    _runner_note_push_failure "${2:-unknown}"
264	    return 0
265	}
266	
267	# ─── _runner_keep_head_on_branch <state_dir> <stage> (#2264) ─────────────────
268	# A model call can leave HEAD off the run branch; every later commit then lands
269	# on HEAD alone while the branch ref — which pr-open checks out and the post-run
270	# step pushes — falls behind. #1844 run 37066147994 lost its work that way. At
271	# every stage end, put HEAD back on the branch when that drops nothing, and say
272	# which stage left it off; when the two diverged, move nothing and say so.
273	_runner_keep_head_on_branch() {
274	    local _stage="${2:-unknown}" _branch="${ZBUILD_RUN_BRANCH:-}"
275	    [[ -n "$_branch" ]] || return 0
276	    local _repo="${ZBUILD_REPO_ROOT:-}"
277	    [[ -n "$_repo" ]] || _repo="$(git rev-parse --show-toplevel 2>/dev/null || true)"
278	    [[ -n "$_repo" ]] || return 0
279	    zbuild_keep_head_on_branch "$_repo" "$_branch"
280	    case "$ZBUILD_HEAD_OUTCOME" in
281	        reattached)
282	            eb_emit_event "pipeline.head.reattached" "stage=$_stage" "branch=$_branch" \
283	                "was=$ZBUILD_HEAD_WAS" 2>/dev/null || true
284	            warn "stage '$_stage' left HEAD off the run branch ($ZBUILD_HEAD_WAS) — moved '$_branch' to HEAD" ;;
285	        diverged)
286	            eb_emit_event "pipeline.head.diverged" "stage=$_stage" "branch=$_branch" \
287	                "was=$ZBUILD_HEAD_WAS" 2>/dev/null || true
288	            warn "stage '$_stage' left HEAD off the run branch and the two diverged — '$_branch' not moved" ;;
289	    esac
290	    return 0
291	}
292	
293	# ─── _runner_snapshot_artifacts <state_dir> <stage> (ADR-050, #1581/#1878) ───
294	# Snapshot the artifact area onto the state branch at a stage boundary, so a
295	# completed stage's work survives a mid-run crash/rate-limit and is available to
296	# the next run. Stage-agnostic (snapshots whatever files exist) and advisory —
297	# never blocks a run.
298	#
299	# #1878: ONE definition, called from every stage-completion site on the LIVE
300	# dispatch-unit path. It previously existed only inline in the legacy linear stage
301	# loop below — which no shipped template ever reaches (any cycle/map/parallel unit
302	# sets _run_dispatch_units=1, and every terminal branch of that block returns), so
303	# the snapshot was never invoked at all and the store was always empty. That is
304	# item 1 of #1807.
305	#
306	# #1878: also no longer swallows stderr. A snapshot that fails now says so, with
307	# the failing git operation named, instead of returning 1 into a `2>/dev/null`
308	# and leaving no trace anywhere.
309	_runner_snapshot_artifacts() {
310	    # $1 may be empty: the cycle-orchestrator call site is several frames from
311	    # main(), and relying on main()'s `state_dir` local reaching it through
312	    # dynamic scope is exactly the kind of implicit coupling that makes a call
313	    # site silently no-op. The runner exports the resolved per-run value at
314	    # runner.sh:1739, so fall back to that.
315	    local _snap_state_dir="${1:-}" _snap_stage="${2:-unknown}"
316	    [[ -n "$_snap_state_dir" ]] || _snap_state_dir="${ZBUILD_STATE_DIR:-}"
317	    [[ -n "$_snap_state_dir" ]] || return 0
318	    # Before the identity guard: a --goal or local run needs its branch kept too.
319	    _runner_keep_head_on_branch "$_snap_state_dir" "$_snap_stage"
320	    # #1931: identity, not issue number. `issue > 0` excluded every --goal run
321	    # from the durable store, so nothing was ever snapshotted for one and the
322	    # push had nothing to send.
323	    _artifact_persist_has_identity "$_runner_issue" || return 0
324	
325	    _artifact_persist_snapshot "$_snap_state_dir" "$_runner_issue" || true
326	    case "${_ARTIFACT_PERSIST_LAST_STATUS:-}" in
327	        saved)
328	            eb_emit_event "artifact.snapshot.saved" \
329	                "stage=$_snap_stage" "issue=$_runner_issue" \
330	                "skipped=${_ARTIFACT_PERSIST_LAST_SKIPPED:-0}" 2>/dev/null || true
331	            ;;
332	        failed)
333	            # Loud, not fatal. This event is the whole point of #1878: the defect
334	            # went undiagnosed for the life of the feature because the failure had
335	            # no channel to surface on.
336	            #
337	            # Deduped on the reason. Most failures are a STATIC precondition — no
338	            # resolvable repository, a ref D/F conflict — so they recur identically
339	            # at every stage boundary. Reporting the first occurrence keeps the
340	            # signal; repeating it once per stage is noise that trains an operator
341	            # to ignore the event. A CHANGED reason is always reported.
342	            if [[ "${_ARTIFACT_PERSIST_LAST_REASON:-}" != "${_RUNNER_LAST_SNAPSHOT_FAIL_REASON:-}" ]]; then
343	                _RUNNER_LAST_SNAPSHOT_FAIL_REASON="${_ARTIFACT_PERSIST_LAST_REASON:-unknown}"
344	                eb_emit_event "artifact.snapshot.failed" \
345	                    "stage=$_snap_stage" "issue=$_runner_issue" \
346	                    "reason=${_ARTIFACT_PERSIST_LAST_REASON:-unknown}" 2>/dev/null || true
347	                warn "artifact snapshot failed at stage '$_snap_stage': ${_ARTIFACT_PERSIST_LAST_REASON:-unknown}"
348	            fi
349	            ;;
350	        # empty / unchanged are not failures and are not events: emitting
351	        # `saved` for them is precisely the lie this change removes.
352	        *) : ;;
353	    esac
354	    # #2187: push at the stage end, not only when the run ends — a run killed
355	    # mid-way (job ceiling, SIGKILL) otherwise loses everything since its start.
356	    # Only for a run that declares where its work goes (ZBUILD_WORKSPACE_BRANCH;
357	    # the CI pipeline sets it). A plain local run — and every test — pushes
358	    # nothing here: tests have left state branches in real checkouts, and
359	    # this would put them on origin. The persist stage still pushes at the end.
360	    [[ -n "${ZBUILD_WORKSPACE_BRANCH:-}" ]] || return 0
361	    local _leak=""
362	    if _leak="$(_artifact_persist_find_secret "$_snap_state_dir/artifacts")"; then
363	        _ARTIFACT_PERSIST_LAST_STATUS="failed"
364	        _ARTIFACT_PERSIST_LAST_REASON="refusing to push — artifact looks like it carries a credential (${_leak})"
365	        _runner_note_push_failure "$_snap_stage"
366	        # The scan covers the artifact area, not the working tree: the run's
367	        # code commits still go to the work branch.
368	        _runner_push_work_branch "$_snap_state_dir" "$_snap_stage"
369	        return 0
370	    fi
371	    if [[ "${_ARTIFACT_PERSIST_LAST_STATUS:-}" == "saved" ]]; then
372	        _artifact_persist_push "$_runner_issue" "${ZBUILD_REPO_ROOT:-}" || true
373	        _runner_note_push_failure "$_snap_stage"
374	    fi
375	    _runner_push_work_branch "$_snap_state_dir" "$_snap_stage"
376	    return 0
377	}

446	# Idempotent (clears the pid first) and rc-neutral (`return 0`, every line
447	# tolerant): it runs inside the EXIT trap under `set -e`, and the process exit
448	# status must never depend on GitHub. TERM, bounded wait, KILL backstop.
449	_runner_status_comment_reap() {
450	    local pid="${_RUNNER_STATUS_COMMENT_PID:-}"

459	        done
460	        kill -0 "$pid" 2>/dev/null && kill -KILL "$pid" 2>/dev/null || true
461	    fi
462	    wait "$pid" 2>/dev/null || true
463	    return 0
464	}

467	# Returns ??:??:?? UTC when the underlying clock primitive yields nothing
468	# (defensive — the operator-visible banner still renders without crashing).
469	_runner_now_short() {
470	    local ms; ms="$(_runner_now_ms)"
471	    if [[ -z "$ms" || ! "$ms" =~ ^[0-9]+$ ]]; then
472	        printf '??:??:?? UTC'
473	        return 0
474	    fi
475	    local sec=$(( ms / 1000 ))
476	    local out
477	    # The shell's clock, in UTC (ADR-065 §5); the date forms stay as the fallback.
478	    TZ=UTC printf -v out '%(%H:%M:%S UTC)T' "$sec" 2>/dev/null && [[ -n "$out" ]] && { printf '%s' "$out"; return 0; }
479	    out="$(date -u -r "$sec" +'%H:%M:%S UTC' 2>/dev/null \
480	        || date -u -d "@$sec" +'%H:%M:%S UTC' 2>/dev/null \
481	        || printf '??:??:?? UTC')"
482	    printf '%s' "$out"

485	# ─── _runner_duration_token <stage> (#508) ───────────────────────────────────
486	# Format the elapsed duration since the start cache was populated. Mirrors
487	# stage-io.sh::_stage_io_render_duration's "<N.N>s" for sub-minute durations;
488	# for >= 60 s we use "<m>m<ss>s" so a slow stage doesn't render as "127.4s".
489	# Cache miss → "?s" (no crash).
490	_runner_duration_token() {
491	    local stage="$1"
492	    local start="${_RUNNER_STAGE_START_MS[$stage]:-}"
493	    if [[ -z "$start" || ! "$start" =~ ^[0-9]+$ ]]; then
494	        printf '?s'
495	        return 0
496	    fi
497	    local now; now="$(_runner_now_ms)"
498	    if [[ -z "$now" || ! "$now" =~ ^[0-9]+$ ]]; then
499	        printf '?s'
500	        return 0
501	    fi
502	    local ms=$(( now - start ))
503	    (( ms < 0 )) && ms=0
504	    if (( ms < 60000 )); then
505	        awk -v m="$ms" 'BEGIN{printf "%.1fs", m/1000}'
506	    else
507	        local total_s=$(( ms / 1000 ))
508	        local mins=$(( total_s / 60 ))
509	        local secs=$(( total_s % 60 ))
510	        printf '%dm%02ds' "$mins" "$secs"
511	    fi
512	}

514	# ─── _runner_record_report <state_dir> <stage> <report-json> (#2189) ─────────
515	# Merge one dispatch's report into the run's record, artifacts/stage-reports.json
516	# (under artifacts/ so it is snapshotted and restored with the run): wiring
517	# files are unioned; owned files are kept per reporting stage, so the
518	# deny list can exempt the owner. Engine setup reads THIS record — never a
519	# stage's artifact by name. Best-effort: a failed merge leaves the prior record.
520	# Parallel members record concurrently, so the read-merge-write holds a mkdir
521	# lock (portable; flock is absent on stock macOS) — else a sibling's merge is lost.
522	# A lock left by a killed holder is reclaimed after 10s.
523	_runner_record_report() {
524	    local state_dir="$1" stage="$2" report="${3:-}"
525	    [[ -n "$state_dir" && -n "$stage" && -n "$report" && "$report" != "{}" ]] || return 0
526	    # Most stages report none of the setup fields — skip the lock and the jq fork.
527	    [[ "$report" == *'"owned_files"'* || "$report" == *'"wiring_files"'* ]] || return 0
528	    local rec="$state_dir/artifacts/stage-reports.json" tmp
529	    local lock="$state_dir/.stage-reports.lock" _tries=0
530	    [[ -d "$state_dir/artifacts" ]] || mkdir -p "$state_dir/artifacts" 2>/dev/null || return 0
531	    until mkdir "$lock" 2>/dev/null; do
532	        # A merge takes milliseconds; a lock held 10s belongs to a dead holder.
533	        if (( ++_tries > 200 )); then rmdir "$lock" 2>/dev/null; _tries=0; fi
534	        sleep 0.05
535	    done
536	    [[ -s "$rec" ]] || printf '{}' > "$rec"
537	    tmp="$rec.tmp.$BASHPID"
538	    if jq --arg s "$stage" --argjson r "$report" '
539	            .wiring_files = ((.wiring_files // []) + ($r.wiring_files // []) | unique)
540	          | if ($r.owned_files // null) != null
541	              then .owned_files = ((.owned_files // {}) + {($s): ($r.owned_files | unique)})
542	              else . end' "$rec" > "$tmp" 2>/dev/null; then
543	        mv -f "$tmp" "$rec"
544	    else
545	        rm -f "$tmp"
546	    fi
547	    rmdir "$lock" 2>/dev/null
548	    return 0
549	}

551	# ─── _runner_validate_leaf_resolvability <stages_arr_name> <plugins_root> ─────
552	# ADR-047 §5: the manifest-derived membership fence — the sole membership
553	# enforcement (the old hardcoded-roster fence is deleted, #1299). Every leaf in the
554	# resolved template flow must resolve to a plugin via resolve_stage_plugin
555	# (role-then-id, ADR-042); an unresolved leaf names the id.
556	#
557	# It is a CONTRACT check, so it is gated by the SAME ZBUILD_CONTRACT_VALIDATOR mode
558	# the inter-stage contract-validator uses (they must agree). Load-time membership
559	# enforcement is the ENFORCE-mode job; the opt-out modes (warn/off) skip it — so
560	# this preflight is a TRUE NO-OP whenever enforcement is off and never perturbs the
561	# mock-roster suites that drive runner.sh under warn (they resolve their leaves at
562	# dispatch via mocked plugin_hook_call, not through a real registry):
563	#   - enforce (default, real runs) / unset → ERROR fail-closed (rc=2). This is the
564	#     load-time guarantee that replaces the old canonical membership gate.
565	#   - warn / off (or any unknown mode)     → skip. Dispatch-time resolution
566	#     (resolve_stage_plugin in the stage loop) still fails a genuinely-missing
567	#     plugin mid-run — the backstop for opt-out runs.
568	# Takes the stage array BY NAME to avoid a subshell copy on read.
569	_runner_validate_leaf_resolvability() {
570	    local _arr_name="$1" plugins_root="$2"
571	    # Only enforce gates at load; warn/off/unknown are opt-outs → no-op. (The
572	    # default is enforce, matching contract-validator's default; unknown modes
573	    # degrade to non-enforce, exactly as contract-validator degrades them to warn.)
574	    [[ "${ZBUILD_CONTRACT_VALIDATOR:-enforce}" == "enforce" ]] || return 0
575	    # Validate the array name is a plain identifier before binding the nameref
576	    # below — never bind a name assembled from unvalidated input (Copilot #1290:
577	    # injection footgun). Callers pass a literal ("active_stages"), so a
578	    # non-identifier is a programming error, not runtime data.
579	    if [[ ! "$_arr_name" =~ ^[A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_]*$ ]]; then
580	        error "_runner_validate_leaf_resolvability: invalid array name '${_arr_name}'"
581	        return 1
582	    fi
583	    # bash errors on a nameref that resolves to itself; reject it with our own
584	    # message rather than a raw "circular name reference" from the shell.
585	    if [[ "$_arr_name" == "_stages" ]]; then
586	        error "_runner_validate_leaf_resolvability: array name '_stages' collides with the nameref"
587	        return 1
588	    fi
589	    # Warm the manifest cache in THIS shell before resolving anything. Every
590	    # resolution below reads manifests through `$( )`, and an associative-array
591	    # write inside a command substitution dies with that subshell — so a lazily
592	    # filled cache is never inherited (#1614, the reason yaml_cache_prewarm
593	    # exists and main() calls it at line ~1370).
594	    #
595	    # main() is not the only entry point. Tests source this file and call helpers
596	    # directly, never reaching that prewarm, and then every lookup forks awk:
597	    # template-resolvability-preflight-test.sh made 28,068 yaml_get calls with
598	    # ZERO cache hits, at real 150s / user 52s / sys 81s — kernel time 1.55x
599	    # user, which is process creation, not computation. Prewarming here took it
600	    # to 82.75s with sys 81s -> 45s.
601	    #
602	    # Here and not in setup_test_env: the prewarm costs 1.32s, and 570 test
603	    # files would pay ~747s for it to benefit the few that resolve plugins.
604	    # Measured before choosing the seam.
605	    #
606	    # Idempotent: a second call re-reads the same keys, which are now cache
607	    # hits. Cheap no-op in production, where main() has already warmed it.
608	    if declare -F yaml_cache_prewarm >/dev/null 2>&1; then
609	        yaml_cache_prewarm "$plugins_root"
610	    fi
611	    # Discovery too, for the same reason and in the same shell: it validates
612	    # every manifest on every call (~1.47s even with the yaml cache warm) and
613	    # runs once per leaf. 19 leaves x 2 templates was 38 full re-validations of
614	    # an unchanged tree.
615	    if declare -F discover_plugins >/dev/null 2>&1; then
616	        discover_plugins "$plugins_root" >/dev/null 2>&1 || true
617	    fi
618	    local -n _stages="${_arr_name}"
619	    local _leaf _ok=1
620	    for _leaf in "${_stages[@]+"${_stages[@]}"}"; do
621	        [[ -z "$_leaf" ]] && continue
622	        # A cycle/parallel GROUP id is a composition operator, not a leaf, and is
623	        # not itself a plugin — its members are already flattened into the stage
624	        # list. Skip group ids (their _TPL_STAGE_TYPE_<id> is cycle|parallel).
625	        local _t_var="_TPL_STAGE_TYPE_${_leaf//-/_}"
626	        case "${!_t_var:-leaf}" in
627	            cycle|parallel) continue ;;
628	        esac
629	        if ! resolve_stage_plugin "$_leaf" "$plugins_root" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
630	            error "load_template: stage '${_leaf}' resolves to no plugin (ADR-047 §5: every leaf must resolve via role or id; add a plugin whose provides.role matches, or whose id is '${_leaf}')"
631	            _ok=0
632	        fi
633	    done
634	    [[ $_ok -eq 1 ]]
635	}

637	# ─── _runner_validate_startup_preflight [violation_fixture] (ADR-051 §warn-first) ──
638	# Aggregation SKELETON (#1318 / D1): owns the violations[]/fail_count collection,
639	# the render-all-at-once block (same pattern as _contract_validate_pipeline) and the
640	# warn/enforce/off mode dispatch. Separate gate from _runner_validate_leaf_
641	# resolvability — it covers non-contract elements the DAG validator does not address.
642	#
643	# It deliberately contributes NO checks of its own yet. The concrete producers land
644	# downstream, each against the discriminating fixtures #1605 pre-stages:
645	#   - persona-binding existence (PERSONA_MISSING) → #1320 (D3)
646	#   - requires.plugins resolution (PLUGIN_MISSING) → #1321 (D4)
647	# An earlier draft carried both checks here, untested; the requires.plugins one was
648	# an acknowledged approximation that raised spurious PLUGIN_MISSING for any entry
649	# naming an ordinary plugin. Shipping checks no test discriminates is the green-but-
650	# inert shape #1605 exists to prevent, so they were removed rather than carried.
651	#
652	# Deliberate divergence from _runner_validate_leaf_resolvability: the DEFAULT mode
653	# here is WARN (not enforce). This lands warn-first so operators see failures before
654	# enforcement is mandatory. Set ZBUILD_CONTRACT_VALIDATOR=enforce to fail-closed.
655	# ZBUILD_CONTRACT_VALIDATOR=off is a full no-op (skips all checks, emits nothing).
656	#
657	# The optional first argument is a synthetic violation fixture: it injects one
658	# pre-formed violation so the aggregation, rendering and mode dispatch are testable
659	# before any real producer exists. A non-empty string yields exactly one violation;
660	# empty (or omitted) yields none. Runtime call sites in runner.sh pass no argument,
661	# so until D3/D4 land the live path always renders nothing and returns 0.
662	# _runner_template_personas <template> — every persona the template names, one
663	# "<where>|<persona id>" per line: <where> is the section, or section/element
664	# for a map element's own persona (ADR-051 §2).
665	_runner_template_personas() {
666	    awk '
667	        function indent(s,   i) { i = 0; while (substr(s, i+1, 1) == " ") i++; return i }
668	        /^[[:space:]]*#/ { next }
669	        /^[A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_-]*:/ { sec = $0; sub(/:.*/, "", sec); el = ""; els_ind = -1; next }
670	        /^[[:space:]]+elements:[[:space:]]*$/ { els_ind = indent($0); next }
671	        els_ind >= 0 && /[^[:space:]]/ && indent($0) <= els_ind { els_ind = -1; el = "" }
672	        els_ind >= 0 && /^[[:space:]]+-[[:space:]]/ {
673	            el = $0; sub(/^[[:space:]]+-[[:space:]]+/, "", el); sub(/^id:[[:space:]]*/, "", el)
674	            sub(/[[:space:]]*#.*/, "", el); gsub(/[[:space:]]/, "", el); next
675	        }
676	        /^[[:space:]]+persona:[[:space:]]*[^[:space:]#]/ {
677	            id = $0; sub(/^[[:space:]]+persona:[[:space:]]*/, "", id); sub(/[[:space:]]*#.*/, "", id)
678	            gsub(/[[:space:]"\047]/, "", id)
679	            print (el != "" ? sec "/" el : sec) "|" id
680	        }
681	    ' "$1" 2>/dev/null
682	}

684	# shellcheck disable=SC2120  # $1 is used by unit tests; runtime call sites pass no arg
685	_runner_validate_startup_preflight() {
686	    local _violation_fixture="${1:-}"
687	    local mode="${ZBUILD_CONTRACT_VALIDATOR:-warn}"
688	    case "$mode" in
689	        warn|enforce|off) ;;
690	        *) mode="warn" ;;
691	    esac
692	
693	    # off = complete no-op, no output
694	    [[ "$mode" == "off" ]] && return 0
695	
696	    local -a violations=()
697	    local fail_count=0
698	
699	    # Synthetic violation fixture for unit tests — non-empty arg injects one violation.
700	    if [[ -n "$_violation_fixture" ]]; then
701	        violations+=("${_violation_fixture}|SYNTHETIC|fixture|synthetic violation injected by test fixture")

703	    fi
704	
705	    # ADR-051 §2 (amended 2026-10-12): every persona the template names — a
706	    # stage's pin, a map element's, the config default — exists in the target
707	    # repository's .zbuild/plugins/persona or the install. A misspelt persona
708	    # must not quietly run as generic, so this refuses in warn mode too.
709	    local _persona_missing=0 _pw _pid _pdir
710	    if [[ -n "${_TPL_SOURCE_FILE:-}" && -f "$_TPL_SOURCE_FILE" ]]; then
711	        # shellcheck source=/dev/null  # followed, it re-reads runner.sh's own includes
712	        declare -F persona_find_dir >/dev/null 2>&1 \
713	            || source "$_ZBUILD_ROOT/scripts/lib/persona-resolve.sh" 2>/dev/null || true
714	        while IFS='|' read -r _pw _pid; do
715	            [[ -n "$_pid" ]] || continue
716	            _pdir="$(persona_find_dir "$_pid" 2>/dev/null)" && [[ -n "$_pdir" ]] && continue
717	            violations+=("${_pw}|PERSONA_MISSING|${_pid}|the template names persona '${_pid}', which is in neither the repository's .zbuild/plugins/persona nor the install")
718	            fail_count=$((fail_count + 1)); _persona_missing=1
719	        done < <(_runner_template_personas "$_TPL_SOURCE_FILE")
720	    fi

722	    # ADR-017 §12 (#2507): every tool word of every stage's calls — the
723	    # install's and the repository's — is one its provider can supply. A call
724	    # that would run without a tool it needs refuses the run, in warn mode too.
725	    local _tools_bad=0 _tw _tl
726	    declare -F route_calls_unsupported_v >/dev/null 2>&1 \
727	        || source "$_ZBUILD_ROOT/core/router/call-tools.sh" 2>/dev/null || true
728	    if declare -F route_calls_unsupported_v >/dev/null 2>&1; then
729	        local -a _tmfs=("$_ZBUILD_ROOT"/plugins/*/*/manifest.yaml)
730	        [[ -n "${ZBUILD_REPO_ROOT:-}" && -d "$ZBUILD_REPO_ROOT/.zbuild/plugins" ]] \
731	            && _tmfs+=("$ZBUILD_REPO_ROOT"/.zbuild/plugins/*/*/manifest.yaml)
732	        route_calls_unsupported_v _tw "${ZBUILD_MODELS_FILE:-$_ZBUILD_ROOT/config/models.json}" "${_tmfs[@]}"
733	        while IFS= read -r _tl; do
734	            [[ -n "$_tl" ]] || continue
735	            local _tr="${_tl#* call }"

800	_runner_pipeline_duration_token() {

802	    if [[ -z "$start" || ! "$start" =~ ^[0-9]+$ ]]; then
803	        printf '?s'
804	        return 0
805	    fi

808	        printf '?s'

813	    if (( ms < 60000 )); then
814	        awk -v m="$ms" 'BEGIN{printf "%.1fs", m/1000}'

816	        local total_s=$(( ms / 1000 ))
817	        local mins=$(( total_s / 60 ))
818	        local secs=$(( total_s % 60 ))

861	# ─── _render_pipeline_end <status> [stage] [rc] (#525) ───────────────────────
862	# Emits the terminal banner that closes a pipeline run, framed with ═ (U+2550)
863	# to distinguish the pipeline boundary from the stage divider (━) and stage-io
864	# banners (─). Two-line layout:
865	#
866	#   ════════════════ pipeline.end ════════════════ HH:MM:SS UTC
867	#   <glyph> Pipeline <status_word>: status=<X> run_id=<Y> issue=<N> (took <dur>)
868	#
869	# Frame bars colored BLUE (chrome). Glyph + leading status word inherit the
870	# verdict class color (foreground signal). Right-aligned timestamp via the
871	# same width math as _render_stage_divider — degrades to a symmetric divider
872	# (no timestamp) when mid_bar <= 2.
873	#
874	# Writes to fd 2 so it composes correctly with other operator lines (info /
875	# success / error) under the same output redirection rules. Banner is emitted
876	# AFTER the pipeline.end JSONL event so the durable event is fail-closed
877	# against banner-write failures.
878	# _runner_restore_stderr — point fd 2 back at the runner's own stderr, saved at
879	# startup in _RUNNER_ERR_FD (ADR-054 §7). A trap that fires inside a call made
880	# with 2>/dev/null runs under that redirect, so the abort banner went to
881	# /dev/null when SIGTERM landed during one. A no-op when nothing was saved.
882	_runner_restore_stderr() {
883	    # Guard against a repeat signal (e.g. `timeout` forwarding its own SIGTERM
884	    # to the process group after the first already fired). Called only from
885	    # _runner_abort_trap (EXIT trap). Setting the guard here — as the very first
886	    # instruction inside the function body — closes the race window that exists
887	    # AFTER this function returns to _runner_abort_trap: bash checks pending
888	    # signals at function-return boundaries, so a pending second TERM would fire
889	    # _runner_signal_trap TERM (→ exit 1) before the explicit guard in
890	    # _runner_abort_trap could execute. By setting it HERE the guard is already
891	    # active by the time the function returns. B3 is satisfied because
892	    # _runner_restore_stderr is still the first call in _runner_abort_trap.
893	    # Ignored, not trapped with ':' (#2493): a handler run inside the trap broke
894	    # it off on bash 5.2, and a TERM to the group ended the trap's own command
895	    # substitutions, which take the default TERM.
896	    trap '' INT TERM
897	    [[ -n "${_RUNNER_ERR_FD:-}" ]] && exec 2>&"$_RUNNER_ERR_FD"
898	    return 0
899	}

901	_render_pipeline_end() {
902	    local status="${1:-unknown}"
903	    local stage_hint="${2:-}"
904	    local rc_hint="${3:-}"
905	    local run_id="${_runner_run_id:-?}"
906	    local issue="${_runner_issue:-?}"
907	    # Best-effort value gathering. Each `$(...)` here forks a helper that may
908	    # itself fork an external (awk in the duration token, date/tput in the
909	    # clock/width helpers). Most call sites invoke this banner DIRECTLY under the
910	    # runner's `set -e` (e.g. the cycle/stage abort + LLM/scope-abort paths) —
911	    # not wrapped in `|| true` — so a transient under-load fork failure in any
912	    # one of these bare assignments would trip errexit and abort the render
913	    # BEFORE the printf block, silently dropping the operator's terminal banner
914	    # mid-teardown. `|| fallback` neutralizes errexit at each assignment so the
915	    # banner is always emitted once the function is reached, on every call site.
916	    # (#1156)
917	    local dur; dur="$(_runner_pipeline_duration_token)" || dur='?s'
918	    local glyph; glyph="$(_pipeline_status_glyph "$status")" || glyph='✗'
919	    local color; color="$(_pipeline_status_color "$status")" || color=''
920	    local frame="${BLUE:-}"
921	    local ts; ts="$(_runner_now_short)" || ts='??:??:?? UTC'
922	    local width; width="$(_term_width)" || width=80
923	
924	    # Map status → operator-friendly verb for line 2. Tracks event payload
925	    # verbatim so "status=<X>" agrees with the verb. ("success" in legacy
926	    # event payloads renders as "complete" — see ADR-015 §v5 amendment).
927	    local word
928	    case "$status" in
929	        success|complete)        word="complete" ;;
930	        complete_unconverged)    word="complete_unconverged" ;;
931	        failed)                  word="failed" ;;
932	        interrupted)             word="interrupted" ;;
933	        aborted)                 word="aborted" ;;
934	        timed_out)               word="timed_out" ;;
935	        preflight_failed)        word="preflight_failed" ;;
936	        *)                       word="$status" ;;
937	    esac
938	
939	    local label=" pipeline.end "
940	    # Layout: <left_bar><label><mid_bar> <ts>
941	    local left_bar=$(( (width - ${#label} - ${#ts} - 1) / 2 ))
942	    local mid_bar=$(( width - left_bar - ${#label} - ${#ts} - 1 ))
943	
944	    local detail_status="status=${status}"
945	    [[ -n "$stage_hint" ]] && detail_status+=" stage=${stage_hint}"
946	    [[ -n "$rc_hint"    ]] && detail_status+=" rc=${rc_hint}"
947	
948	    if [[ "$mid_bar" -le 2 ]]; then
949	        # Degraded layout — drop timestamp from the header.
950	        local sides=$(( (width - ${#label}) / 2 ))
951	        [[ "$sides" -lt 2 ]] && sides=2
952	        local bar
953	        printf -v bar '%*s' "$sides" ''
954	        bar="${bar// /═}"
955	        {
956	            printf '\n'
957	            printf '%b%s%b%s%b%b%s%b\n' "$frame" "$bar" "${BOLD:-}" "$label" "${RESET:-}" "$frame" "$bar" "${RESET:-}"
958	            printf '%b%b%s%b Pipeline %s: %s run_id=%s issue=%s (took %s)\n' \
959	                "$color" "${BOLD:-}" "$glyph" "${RESET:-}" \
960	                "$word" "$detail_status" "$run_id" "$issue" "$dur"
961	        } >&2
962	        _runner_render_open_items "$status" || true
963	        return 0
964	    fi
965	
966	    local lbar rbar
967	    printf -v lbar '%*s' "$left_bar" ''; lbar="${lbar// /═}"
968	    printf -v rbar '%*s' "$mid_bar"  ''; rbar="${rbar// /═}"
969	    {
970	        printf '\n'
971	        printf '%b%s%b%s%b%b%s%b %s\n' \
972	            "$frame" "$lbar" "${BOLD:-}" "$label" "${RESET:-}" \
973	            "$frame" "$rbar" "${RESET:-}" "$ts"
974	        printf '%b%b%s%b Pipeline %s: %s run_id=%s issue=%s (took %s)\n' \
975	            "$color" "${BOLD:-}" "$glyph" "${RESET:-}" \
976	            "$word" "$detail_status" "$run_id" "$issue" "$dur"
977	    } >&2
978	    _runner_render_open_items "$status" || true
979	}

981	# _runner_render_open_items <status> — #2330 (ADR-068 §8): a run that did not

983	# settle it. pipeline.end keeps the engine's code; this is what a reader sees.
984	_runner_render_open_items() {

1001	# ─── _render_stage_divider <stage> (#492, ts: #508) ──────────────────────────
1002	# Emits a blank line + a heavy horizontal rule (━ U+2501) with the stage name

1023	    local ts; ts="$(_runner_now_short)"
1024

1038	            printf '\n'
1039	            printf '%b%s%b%s%b%b%s%b\n' "$color" "$bar" "${BOLD:-}" "$label" "${RESET:-}" "$color" "$bar" "${RESET:-}"

1067	# ─── Cycle banner helpers (#524, ADR-015 §v6, ADR-021) ───────────────────────
1068	# Operator-fd-2 chrome for outer cycles (ADR-021). These render a visual
1069	# hierarchy that nests cleanly with the existing stage-transition divider
1070	# (_render_stage_divider) so the operator can see cycle entry, per-iter
1071	# boundaries, per-iter outcomes, and cycle exit in the scrollback.
1072	#
1073	# Glyph + color ladder (heaviest → lightest):
1074	#   ━━━ (U+2501) stage transition   — BOLD BLUE (handled in _render_stage_divider)
1075	#   ═══ (U+2550) cycle entry/exit   — LIGHT_BLUE
1076	#   ─── (U+2500) cycle iter divider — CYAN

1079	#   - All 4 helpers write to fd 2 ONLY. Hardcoded `>&2`. NEVER capture in $(…)

1081	#     banner=best-effort).
1082	#   - `{ ...; } >&2 2>/dev/null || true` is used so a broken stderr can never
1083	#     abort the cycle. Each block is a single printf wrapped in the redirect
1084	#     group so SIGINT during banner emit cannot race on partial writes.
1085	#   - These banners are fd-2 ONLY and NEVER appear in the PR comment body
1086	#     rendered by gh_comment. Operator chrome only.

1088	# Determinism: honors ZBUILD_TERM_WIDTH_OVERRIDE + ZBUILD_STAGE_IO_NOW_MS_OVERRIDE
1089	# via _term_width / _runner_now_short (same contract as _render_stage_divider).

1094	# operator's eye finds the cycle boundary before the first iter divider.

1097	    local width; width="$(_term_width)"

1100	    [[ "$sides" -lt 2 ]] && sides=2
1101	    local bar
1102	    printf -v bar '%*s' "$sides" ''
1103	    bar="${bar// /═}"
1104	    {
1105	        printf '\n'
1106	        printf '%b%s%b%s%b%b%s%b\n' \
1107	            "${LIGHT_BLUE:-}" "$bar" "${BOLD:-}" "$label" "${RESET:-}" \
1108	            "${LIGHT_BLUE:-}" "$bar" "${RESET:-}"
1109	        printf '%b%b▸%b Entering cycle: %b%b%s%b\n' \
1110	            "${LIGHT_BLUE:-}" "${BOLD:-}" "${RESET:-}" \

1170	# glance which outer iter this divider belongs to:
1171	#   outer (no prefix): `─── build_review_cycle iter 1/2 ───`
1172	#   inner (prefix set): `─── [4.1] build_test_cycle iter 1/3 ───`
1173	# Reuses the seq-prefix machinery from Wave 19-B #718 / cycle-orchestrator.sh:888
1174	# — no new plumbing, no hook-signature change. Emitted by the orchestrator's
1175	# iter-begin hook BEFORE the first per-stage banner of the iter.
1176	_render_cycle_iter_divider() {
1177	    local cycle_id="$1" iter="$2" max="$3"
1178	    local prefix="${ZBUILD_SEQ_PREFIX:-}"
1179	    local label
1180	    if [[ -n "$prefix" ]]; then
1181	        label=" [${prefix}] ${cycle_id} iter ${iter}/${max} "
1182	    else
1183	        label=" ${cycle_id} iter ${iter}/${max} "
1184	    fi
1185	    local width; width="$(_term_width)"
1186	    local sides=$(( (width - ${#label}) / 2 ))
1187	    [[ "$sides" -lt 2 ]] && sides=2
1188	    local bar
1189	    printf -v bar '%*s' "$sides" ''
1190	    bar="${bar// /─}"
1191	    {
1192	        printf '\n%b%s%b%s%b%b%s%b\n' \
1193	            "${CYAN:-}" "$bar" "${BOLD:-}" "$label" "${RESET:-}" \
1194	            "${CYAN:-}" "$bar" "${RESET:-}"
1195	    } >&2 2>/dev/null || true
1196	}
1197	
1198	# ─── _render_cycle_iter_complete <iter> <verdict> <score> <fc> <elapsed_s> ──
1199	# Per-iter DIM trailer line e.g. `↳ iter 2 complete: verdict=pass score=-1
1200	# failure_count=1 elapsed=4s`. Emitted by the orchestrator's iter-complete
1201	# hook AFTER the `cycle.iteration.complete` event is durable. #1254: the
1202	# `score` axis (progress − defects) replaced the retired `velocity` label so
1203	# the per-iter line matches the OUTPUT banner's health score.
1204	_render_cycle_iter_complete() {
1205	    local iter="$1" verdict="$2" score="$3" failure_count="$4" elapsed_s="$5"
1206	    {
1207	        printf '%b↳ iter %s complete: verdict=%s score=%s failure_count=%s elapsed=%ss%b\n' \
1208	            "${DIM:-}" "$iter" "$verdict" "$score" "$failure_count" "$elapsed_s" "${RESET:-}"
1209	    } >&2 2>/dev/null || true
1210	}
1211	
1212	# ─── _render_cycle_exit <cycle_id> <reason> <iter> <max> ──────────────────────
1213	# Heavy `═` LIGHT_BLUE divider + verdict-glyph line mapping termination reason
1214	# to glyph + color (see #524 spec).
1215	#   converged       → ✓ GREEN+BOLD
1216	#   max_iterations  → ✗ RED+BOLD
1217	#   plateau         → ✗ RED+BOLD

1	#!/usr/bin/env bash
2	# core/pipeline/cycle-orchestrator.sh — ADR-021 outer-cycle orchestrator (F1)
3	#
4	# F1 = foundational framework + flag-gated stub. NO concrete cycle wired in
5	# config/templates/standard.yaml (F2/#511 does that). Runner only enters the
6	# cycle branch when ZBUILD_CYCLES_ENABLED=1 AND a `cycles:` overlay is parsed.
7	#
8	# Public surface:
9	#   cycle_orchestrator_run <cycle_id> <state_dir> <state_file>
10	#     rc: 0=converged, 1=max_iterations, 2=plateau, 3=divergence,
11	#         130=aborted, 4=config_invalid (template error)
12	#     Sets globals:
13	#       _CYCLE_LAST_TERMINATED_REASON  string enum
14	#       _CYCLE_LAST_ITERATIONS         int
15	#       _CYCLE_LAST_HISTORY_FILE       absolute path
16	#       _CYCLE_LAST_MEMBER_HALT        "<word>: <reason>" when a member's result
17	#                                      halted the run (ADR-068 §3), else empty
18	#
19	# Internal helpers (prefix `_cycle_`):
20	#   _cycle_load_template / _cycle_iter_dispatch / _cycle_install_traps /
21	#   _cycle_clear_traps   / _cycle_on_signal     / _cycle_record_iter_outcome /
22	#   _cycle_check_until   / _cycle_check_max_iterations /
23	#   _cycle_detect_plateau / _cycle_detect_divergence /
24	#   _cycle_apply_feedback / _cycle_handle_terminal
25	#
26	# Sourced library: do not add `set -euo pipefail` here.
27	
28	[[ -n "${_ZBUILD_CYCLE_ORCH_LOADED:-}" ]] && return 0
29	_ZBUILD_CYCLE_ORCH_LOADED=1
30	
31	_CYCLE_ORCH_DIR="$(cd "${BASH_SOURCE[0]%/*}" 2>/dev/null || true; pwd)"
32	_CYCLE_ORCH_ROOT="$(cd "$_CYCLE_ORCH_DIR/../.." && pwd)"
33	
34	# shellcheck source=../../scripts/lib/helpers.sh
35	source "$_CYCLE_ORCH_ROOT/scripts/lib/helpers.sh"
36	# ADR-025 (Wave 15-B #684) abort-propagation contract helpers.
37	# shellcheck source=../../scripts/lib/abort-propagation.sh
38	source "$_CYCLE_ORCH_ROOT/scripts/lib/abort-propagation.sh"
39	# shellcheck source=../state/atomic.sh
40	source "$_CYCLE_ORCH_ROOT/core/state/atomic.sh"
41	# shellcheck source=../state/resume.sh
42	source "$_CYCLE_ORCH_ROOT/core/state/resume.sh"
43	# shellcheck source=../event-bus/event-bus.sh
44	source "$_CYCLE_ORCH_ROOT/core/event-bus/event-bus.sh"
45	# shellcheck source=./template.sh
46	source "$_CYCLE_ORCH_ROOT/core/pipeline/template.sh"
47	# shellcheck source=../output/event-banners.sh
48	# #526: operator-visible WARN banner for HIGH-severity cycle events.
49	source "$_CYCLE_ORCH_ROOT/core/output/event-banners.sh"
50	# #833: cycle INPUT/OUTPUT boundary banners go through the stage-io chokepoint
51	# (kind=cycle). The runner's main process does NOT otherwise source stage-io
52	# (only plugin subshells do, via route.sh), so source it here. stage-io.sh has
53	# its own load guard, so this is a no-op when already sourced.
54	# shellcheck source=../output/stage-io.sh
55	source "$_CYCLE_ORCH_ROOT/core/output/stage-io.sh"
56	# #511 F2 Pin 2: resolve feedback source paths via the from-stage manifest's
57	# outputs[id==<X>].path entry (so the orchestrator stops assuming the legacy
58	# `artifacts/<stage>/<output>` layout that real plugins do NOT follow).
59	# shellcheck source=../../scripts/lib/manifest-graph.sh
60	source "$_CYCLE_ORCH_ROOT/scripts/lib/manifest-graph.sh"
61	# ADR-039 (#1132): a cycle member may be a `type: parallel` group — dispatch it
62	# via the A2 parallel orchestrator. Load guard makes this a no-op when already
63	# sourced; parallel-orchestrator.sh does NOT source us back (no cycle).
64	# shellcheck source=./parallel-orchestrator.sh
65	source "$_CYCLE_ORCH_ROOT/core/pipeline/parallel-orchestrator.sh"
66	# #1822: the disposition response table, for the dispatch event.
67	# shellcheck source=./disposition.sh
68	source "$_CYCLE_ORCH_ROOT/core/pipeline/disposition.sh"
69	
70	# ─── Constants ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
71	# HARDCODED ceiling — checked BEFORE the template's max_iterations value (silent-
72	# failure guard #2). Templates that ask for more get clamped + emit config.invalid.
73	readonly _CYCLE_ABSOLUTE_MAX=10
74	
75	# Default convergence-detection windows (overridable per cycle in template).
76	readonly _CYCLE_DEFAULT_PLATEAU_WINDOW=3
77	readonly _CYCLE_DEFAULT_DIVERGENCE_WINDOW=2
78	
79	# ─── Public globals (set by cycle_orchestrator_run) ──────────────────────────
80	_CYCLE_LAST_TERMINATED_REASON=""
81	_CYCLE_LAST_ITERATIONS=0
82	_CYCLE_LAST_HISTORY_FILE=""
83	_CYCLE_LAST_MEMBER_HALT=""
84	_CYCLE_VELOCITY_PLATEAU_WINDOW=0  # 0 = disabled until template sets velocity_plateau.window
85	_CYCLE_LAST_PLATEAU_EVIDENCE=""
86	
87	# #1284 (ADR-047): multi-condition exit_when state — populated by _cycle_load_template.
88	# Empty combinator means single-condition mode (byte-identical behavior).
89	_CYCLE_EXIT_COMBINATOR=""
90	_CYCLE_EXIT_CONDITIONS=()
91	
92	# #2325 (ADR-063 §5): how many loops this one is nested inside. Only the
93	# outermost loop (depth 0) publishes ZBUILD_OUTER_ROUND, so a stage knows which
94	# outer round it runs in even though an inner loop restarts its own counter at
95	# round 1 each outer round (ADR-068 §2). (The notes label that read it was
96	# withdrawn, ADR-063 §5 amended 2026-10-12; it stays published for the run's
97	# own record.)
98	_CYCLE_NEST_DEPTH=0
99	
100	# #833: last-evaluated termination predicate, stashed by _cycle_check_until /
101	# _cycle_check_abort_when, read by _cycle_render_predicate_result for the
102	# cycle OUTPUT banner. kind = exit_when | abort_when.
103	_CYCLE_LAST_PREDICATE_KIND=""
104	_CYCLE_LAST_PREDICATE_STAGE=""
105	_CYCLE_LAST_PREDICATE_FIELD=""
106	_CYCLE_LAST_PREDICATE_OP=""
107	_CYCLE_LAST_PREDICATE_EXPECTED=""
108	_CYCLE_LAST_PREDICATE_ACTUAL=""
109	_CYCLE_LAST_PREDICATE_MATCH=""
110	
111	# #833: per-iter cycle-banner seq counters, keyed by iter. Holds the reserved
112	# seq from stage_io_begin so the matching stage_io_end can pair correctly.
113	declare -gA _CYCLE_IO_SEQ=()
114	
115	# Internal trap-state (mirrors _route_loop_* convention in route.sh).
116	_CYCLE_TRAP_CYCLE_ID=""
117	_CYCLE_TRAP_ITER=0
118	_CYCLE_TRAP_HISTORY_FILE=""
119	
120	# ADR-029 G2 (#810): per-member consecutive router-timeout counter.
121	# Resets on every cycle_orchestrator_run entry. Incremented when a leaf
122	# member returns verdict=error reason=router_timeout|router_oom_kill;
123	# zeroed on any non-timeout dispatch.
124	declare -gA _CYCLE_TIMEOUT_RUN=()
125	
126	# ADR-029 G3 (#812): per-member max_turns base captured at the FIRST timeout.
127	# Stores the original (pre-bump) budget so escalation math stays anchored
128	# even after the override is in effect. Reset on success.
129	declare -gA _CYCLE_TURNS_BASE=()
130	
131	# ADR-029 G2/G3 cross-iteration persistence (#844): keyed by cycle_id:stage_name.
132	# Survive cycle_orchestrator_run re-entry for nested invocations of the same
133	# cycle_id so stages that burned timeout budget carry their count forward.
134	declare -gA _CYCLE_TIMEOUT_RUN_PERSIST=()
135	declare -gA _CYCLE_TURNS_BASE_PERSIST=()
136	
137	# ─── Per-iter start-wall-clock cache (#524) ──────────────────────────────────
138	# Populated by the iter-begin hook (orchestrator) and read by the iter-complete
139	# hook to compute elapsed_s for the operator-visible iter-complete trailer.
140	# Keyed by iter number; values are ms epochs.
141	declare -gA _CYCLE_ITER_START_MS=()
142	
143	# ─── _cycle_emit — wrapper around eb_emit_event with cycle envelope ──────────
144	# Adds cycle_id automatically; payload is flat k=v per zbuild convention.
145	# #526: also dispatches to the HIGH-event banner emitter so the 5 high-severity
146	# cycle.* events fire both a JSONL record (durable) AND a stderr WARN banner
147	# (operator-visible). Banner is a no-op for non-HIGH event types — see
148	# core/output/event-banners.sh::_HIGH_EVENT_TYPES.
149	_cycle_emit() {
150	    local type="$1"; shift
151	    eb_emit_event "$type" "cycle_id=${_CYCLE_TRAP_CYCLE_ID:-unknown}" "$@" \
152	        2>/dev/null || true
153	    # Banner intentionally writes to stderr — do NOT redirect 2>/dev/null here.
154	    # The helper itself wraps its body in best-effort guards.
155	    _emit_high_event_banner "$type" "$@" || true
156	}
157	
158	# Wave 19-C-1 (#725): always-on predicate-evaluation instrumentation. Emitted
159	# from _cycle_check_until (kind=exit_when) and _cycle_check_abort_when
160	# (kind=abort_when) after each evaluation. Lets operators see exactly what
161	# the predicate compared and whether it matched — answering the "did the
162	# predicate even fire?" / "what verdict did it actually see?" forensic
163	# questions without instrumenting the orchestrator post-hoc.
164	_cycle_emit_predicate() {
165	    local kind="$1" stage="$2" field="$3" op="$4" expected="$5" actual="$6" match="$7"
166	    eb_emit_event "cycle.predicate.evaluated" \
167	        "cycle_id=${_CYCLE_TRAP_CYCLE_ID:-unknown}" \
168	        "iter=${_CYCLE_TRAP_ITER:-0}" \
169	        "kind=$kind" "stage=$stage" "field=$field" "op=$op" \
170	        "expected=$expected" "actual=$actual" "match=$match" \
171	        2>/dev/null || true
172	}
173	
174	# Wave 19-D-1 (#731): per-member dispatch instrumentation. Emitted by
175	# _cycle_iter_dispatch at the start of each member's dispatch (BEFORE the
176	# nested-cycle recursion or leaf cycle_dispatch_stage call) and at the
177	# complete boundary (AFTER rc is captured and verdict is mapped). Answers
178	# "did the for-loop reach member X?" deterministically from events.jsonl —
179	# without these, the dogfood 20260605140602-80831 forensics required
180	# code-reading to deduce that review was never dispatched.
181	_cycle_emit_member_dispatch_start() {
182	    local position="$1" member="$2" kind="$3"
183	    eb_emit_event "cycle.member.dispatch.start" \
184	        "cycle_id=${_CYCLE_TRAP_CYCLE_ID:-unknown}" \
185	        "iter=${_CYCLE_TRAP_ITER:-0}" \
186	        "position=$position" "member=$member" "kind=$kind" \
187	        2>/dev/null || true
188	}
189	
190	# #1822 (ADR-054 §6): the dispatch event carries the resolved `disposition` and the
191	# engine's response to it, so an operator can see WHY a stage was treated as
192	# recoverable — or why it was not — without inferring it from an rc.
193	#
194	# Read off the _CYCLE_DISPATCH_DISPOSITION channel rather than taken as a sixth
195	# positional arg: this function has nine call sites, most of them abort paths
196	# that have no disposition to pass, and the channel is how cycle_id/iter already
197	# reach here. An empty value is reported as empty — a v1 stage declares no
198	# disposition, and the event must not invent one.
199	_cycle_emit_member_dispatch_complete() {
200	    local position="$1" member="$2" rc="$3" verdict="$4" status="$5"
201	    local _disp="${_CYCLE_DISPATCH_DISPOSITION:-}" _disp_resp=""
202	    # Spelled as an `if` rather than `[[ ... ]] && ...`: under errexit a failing
203	    # && list is only safe because another command follows it, which is a
204	    # property of the surrounding code rather than of this line.
205	    if [[ -n "$_disp" ]]; then
206	        _disp_resp="$(disposition_response "$_disp" 2>/dev/null || true)"
207	    fi
208	    eb_emit_event "cycle.member.dispatch.complete" \
209	        "cycle_id=${_CYCLE_TRAP_CYCLE_ID:-unknown}" \
210	        "iter=${_CYCLE_TRAP_ITER:-0}" \
211	        "position=$position" "member=$member" \
212	        "rc=$rc" "verdict=$verdict" "status=$status" \
213	        "disposition=$_disp" "disposition_response=$_disp_resp" \
214	        2>/dev/null || true
215	
216	    # ADR-050 (#1878): a cycle member is a stage boundary, and this is the single
217	    # funnel every member completion passes through. The snapshot used to live
218	    # only on the LEAF path in runner.sh, so `design`, `build` and `test` — most
219	    # of a real run's output under simple.yaml — were never persisted at all.
220	    #
221	    # Every member, whatever its rc (#2187): a failed or timed-out member's
222	    # outputs are what the next session needs most — #1849's test-author ran
223	    # twice, failed, and was never snapshotted. The abort paths (6/130/143)
224	    # route through here too, and saving their work on the way out is the point.
225	    : "$rc"
226	    if declare -F _runner_snapshot_artifacts >/dev/null 2>&1; then
227	        _runner_snapshot_artifacts "" "$member"
228	    fi
229	}
230	
231	# ─── Trap composition (silent-failure findings #5, #6) ───────────────────────
232	# Cycle owns ONLY INT/TERM. Runner owns EXIT. On signal: record the abort word
233	# (ADR-025 — the next dispatch boundary sees it), emit cycle.aborted, clear
234	# traps. Must be re-installed after each stage dispatch because
235	# route.sh::_route_loop_install_traps clobbers without saving.
236	_cycle_install_traps() {
237	    trap '_cycle_on_signal SIGINT' INT
238	    trap '_cycle_on_signal SIGTERM' TERM
239	}
240	_cycle_clear_traps() {
241	    trap - INT TERM
242	}
243	_cycle_on_signal() {
244	    # ADR-054 §7 (#2493): a repeat signal is ignored while this runs, never
245	    # handled inside it (on bash 5.2 that broke this handler off part-way).
246	    trap '' INT TERM
247	    local sig="$1" word="sigint"
248	    [[ "$sig" == "SIGTERM" ]] && word="sigterm"
249	    _zbuild_arm_abort_sentinel "$word"
250	    # ADR-054 §7: the member running now is stopped, not waited out.
251	    declare -F plugin_stop_running >/dev/null 2>&1 && plugin_stop_running
252	    _CYCLE_LAST_TERMINATED_REASON="aborted"
253	    eb_emit_event "cycle.aborted" \
254	        "cycle_id=${_CYCLE_TRAP_CYCLE_ID:-unknown}" \
255	        "iter=${_CYCLE_TRAP_ITER}" \
256	        "signal=$sig" 2>/dev/null || true
257	    _cycle_clear_traps
258	    _CYCLE_TRAP_CYCLE_ID=''
259	}
260	
261	# ─── _cycle_member_is_blocking <stage_id> ────────────────────────────────────
262	# ADR-013 blocking table (CQ-3 / issue #863). Reads the template-parsed
263	# _TPL_STAGE_BLOCKING_<safe_id> export set by template.sh from the `blocking:`
264	# YAML attribute. Returns 0 when the member halts the cycle on failure.
265	_cycle_member_is_blocking() {
266	    local _blk_safe="${1//-/_}"
267	    local _blk_var="_TPL_STAGE_BLOCKING_${_blk_safe}"
268	    [[ "${!_blk_var:-}" == "true" ]]
269	}
270	
271	# ─── _cycle_load_template <cycle_id> ─────────────────────────────────────────
272	# Reads template-parser cycle vars set by template.sh::_tpl_parse_cycle_data.
273	# Validates max_iterations bounds + required fields. Populates:
274	#   _CYCLE_STAGES[]     (contiguous subsequence of canonical stages)
275	#   _CYCLE_MAX_ITER     (integer 1.._CYCLE_ABSOLUTE_MAX)
276	#   _CYCLE_ON_MAX       (continue|halt)
277	#   _CYCLE_UNTIL_STAGE  (id within _CYCLE_STAGES)
278	#   _CYCLE_UNTIL_FIELD  (verdict|status)
279	#   _CYCLE_UNTIL_OP     (one of _TPL_PREDICATE_OPS, ADR-027 §5)
280	#   _CYCLE_UNTIL_VALUE  (string)
281	#   _CYCLE_PLATEAU_WINDOW / _CYCLE_DIVERGENCE_WINDOW / _CYCLE_VELOCITY_PLATEAU_WINDOW
282	# Returns: 0 valid; 1 invalid (emits cycle.config.invalid).
283	_cycle_load_template() {
284	    local cycle_id="$1"
285	    local safe="${cycle_id//-/_}"
286	
287	    _CYCLE_STAGES=()
288	    _CYCLE_MAX_ITER=""
289	    _CYCLE_ON_MAX="continue"
290	    _CYCLE_UNTIL_STAGE=""
291	    _CYCLE_UNTIL_FIELD=""
292	    _CYCLE_UNTIL_OP=""
293	    _CYCLE_UNTIL_VALUE=""
294	    # #1284 (ADR-047): multi-condition exit_when state.
295	    _CYCLE_EXIT_COMBINATOR=""
296	    _CYCLE_EXIT_CONDITIONS=()
297	    _CYCLE_PLATEAU_WINDOW="$_CYCLE_DEFAULT_PLATEAU_WINDOW"
298	    _CYCLE_DIVERGENCE_WINDOW="$_CYCLE_DEFAULT_DIVERGENCE_WINDOW"
299	    _CYCLE_VELOCITY_PLATEAU_WINDOW=0  # 0 = disabled; only set when template has velocity_plateau.window
300	
301	    # Pull from template-parser side-channel vars.
302	    local stages_var="_TPL_CYCLE_STAGES_${safe}"
303	    local max_var="_TPL_CYCLE_MAX_${safe}"
304	    local on_max_var="_TPL_CYCLE_ON_MAX_${safe}"
305	    local us_var="_TPL_CYCLE_UNTIL_STAGE_${safe}"
306	    local uf_var="_TPL_CYCLE_UNTIL_FIELD_${safe}"
307	    local uo_var="_TPL_CYCLE_UNTIL_OP_${safe}"
308	    local uv_var="_TPL_CYCLE_UNTIL_VALUE_${safe}"
309	    local pw_var="_TPL_CYCLE_PLATEAU_W_${safe}"
310	    local dw_var="_TPL_CYCLE_DIVERGENCE_W_${safe}"
311	
312	    local stages_csv="${!stages_var:-}"
313	    if [[ -z "$stages_csv" ]]; then
314	        error "cycle '$cycle_id': no stages declared"
315	        _cycle_emit "cycle.config.invalid" "reason=no_stages"
316	        return 1
317	    fi
318	    local IFS_save="$IFS"; IFS=','
319	    # shellcheck disable=SC2206
320	    _CYCLE_STAGES=($stages_csv)
321	    IFS="$IFS_save"
322	
323	    _CYCLE_MAX_ITER="${!max_var:-}"
324	    if [[ -z "$_CYCLE_MAX_ITER" ]] || ! [[ "$_CYCLE_MAX_ITER" =~ ^[0-9]+$ ]]; then
325	        error "cycle '$cycle_id': max_iterations required (integer 1..${_CYCLE_ABSOLUTE_MAX})"
326	        _cycle_emit "cycle.config.invalid" "reason=max_iterations_missing_or_nonint" \
327	            "value=${_CYCLE_MAX_ITER:-<unset>}"
328	        return 1
329	    fi
330	    if [[ "$_CYCLE_MAX_ITER" -lt 1 || "$_CYCLE_MAX_ITER" -gt "$_CYCLE_ABSOLUTE_MAX" ]]; then
331	        error "cycle '$cycle_id': max_iterations must be 1..${_CYCLE_ABSOLUTE_MAX}, got: $_CYCLE_MAX_ITER"
332	        _cycle_emit "cycle.config.invalid" "reason=max_iterations_out_of_range" \
333	            "value=$_CYCLE_MAX_ITER" "absolute_max=$_CYCLE_ABSOLUTE_MAX"
334	        return 1
335	    fi
336	
337	    _CYCLE_ON_MAX="${!on_max_var:-continue}"
338	    if [[ "$_CYCLE_ON_MAX" != "continue" && "$_CYCLE_ON_MAX" != "halt" ]]; then
339	        error "cycle '$cycle_id': on_max must be continue|halt, got: $_CYCLE_ON_MAX"
340	        _cycle_emit "cycle.config.invalid" "reason=on_max_invalid" \
341	            "value=$_CYCLE_ON_MAX"
342	        return 1
343	    fi
344	
345	    # #1284 (ADR-047): check for multi-condition exit_when first. When present,
346	    # the single-condition _TPL_CYCLE_UNTIL_* vars are empty — skip their validation.
347	    local ew_comb_var="_TPL_CYCLE_EXIT_COMBINATOR_${safe}"
348	    local ew_count_var="_TPL_CYCLE_EXIT_COUNT_${safe}"
349	    _CYCLE_EXIT_COMBINATOR="${!ew_comb_var:-}"
350	    if [[ -n "$_CYCLE_EXIT_COMBINATOR" ]]; then
351	        case "$_CYCLE_EXIT_COMBINATOR" in
352	            all|any) ;;
353	            *)
354	                error "cycle '$cycle_id': exit_when combinator must be all|any, got: $_CYCLE_EXIT_COMBINATOR"
355	                _cycle_emit "cycle.config.invalid" "reason=exit_when_combinator_invalid" \
356	                    "value=$_CYCLE_EXIT_COMBINATOR"
357	                return 1
358	                ;;
359	        esac
360	        local ew_count="${!ew_count_var:-0}"
361	        if ! [[ "$ew_count" =~ ^[0-9]+$ ]] || [[ "$ew_count" -lt 1 ]]; then
362	            error "cycle '$cycle_id': exit_when multi-condition count must be >=1, got: $ew_count"
363	            _cycle_emit "cycle.config.invalid" "reason=exit_when_count_invalid"
364	            return 1
365	        fi
366	        local ew_i ew_s ew_f ew_o ew_v
367	        for (( ew_i=1; ew_i<=ew_count; ew_i++ )); do
368	            local _sv="_TPL_CYCLE_EXIT_${ew_i}_STAGE_${safe}"
369	            local _fv="_TPL_CYCLE_EXIT_${ew_i}_FIELD_${safe}"
370	            local _ov="_TPL_CYCLE_EXIT_${ew_i}_OP_${safe}"
371	            local _vv="_TPL_CYCLE_EXIT_${ew_i}_VALUE_${safe}"
372	            ew_s="${!_sv:-}"; ew_f="${!_fv:-}"; ew_o="${!_ov:-}"; ew_v="${!_vv:-}"
373	            if [[ -z "$ew_s" || -z "$ew_f" || -z "$ew_o" || -z "$ew_v" ]]; then
374	                error "cycle '$cycle_id': exit_when condition $ew_i: {stage,field,op,value} all required"
375	                _cycle_emit "cycle.config.invalid" "reason=exit_when_condition_incomplete" "index=$ew_i"
376	                return 1
377	            fi
378	            case "$ew_f" in
379	                verdict|status) ;;
380	                *)
381	                    error "cycle '$cycle_id': exit_when condition $ew_i: field must be verdict|status, got: $ew_f"
382	                    _cycle_emit "cycle.config.invalid" "reason=exit_when_field_invalid" "value=$ew_f"
383	                    return 1
384	                    ;;
385	            esac
386	            # ADR-027 §5 (#1760): the same rule the template loader applies.
387	            local _ew_pp; _ew_pp="$(_tpl_predicate_problem "$ew_o" "$ew_v")"
388	            if [[ -n "$_ew_pp" ]]; then
389	                error "cycle '$cycle_id': exit_when condition $ew_i (field '$ew_f'): $_ew_pp"
390	                _cycle_emit "cycle.config.invalid" "reason=exit_when_op_invalid" "value=$ew_o"
391	                return 1
392	            fi
393	            local _cs_ok=0 _cs
394	            for _cs in "${_CYCLE_STAGES[@]}"; do
395	                [[ "$_cs" == "$ew_s" ]] && _cs_ok=1 && break
396	            done
397	            if [[ $_cs_ok -ne 1 ]]; then
398	                error "cycle '$cycle_id': exit_when condition $ew_i: stage '$ew_s' is not in cycle stages (${_CYCLE_STAGES[*]})"
399	                _cycle_emit "cycle.config.invalid" "reason=exit_when_stage_outside_cycle" "value=$ew_s"
400	                return 1
401	            fi
402	            _CYCLE_EXIT_CONDITIONS+=("${ew_s}|${ew_f}|${ew_o}|${ew_v}")
403	        done
404	    else
405	        _CYCLE_UNTIL_STAGE="${!us_var:-}"
406	        _CYCLE_UNTIL_FIELD="${!uf_var:-}"
407	        _CYCLE_UNTIL_OP="${!uo_var:-}"
408	        _CYCLE_UNTIL_VALUE="${!uv_var:-}"
409	
410	        if [[ -z "$_CYCLE_UNTIL_STAGE" || -z "$_CYCLE_UNTIL_FIELD" \
411	              || -z "$_CYCLE_UNTIL_OP" || -z "$_CYCLE_UNTIL_VALUE" ]]; then
412	            error "cycle '$cycle_id': until.{stage,field,op,value} all required"
413	            _cycle_emit "cycle.config.invalid" "reason=until_incomplete"
414	            return 1
415	        fi
416	        # v1 whitelist
417	        case "$_CYCLE_UNTIL_FIELD" in
418	            verdict|status) ;;
419	            *)
420	                error "cycle '$cycle_id': until.field must be verdict|status, got: $_CYCLE_UNTIL_FIELD"
421	                _cycle_emit "cycle.config.invalid" "reason=until_field_invalid" \
422	                    "value=$_CYCLE_UNTIL_FIELD"
423	                return 1
424	                ;;
425	        esac
426	        local _u_pp; _u_pp="$(_tpl_predicate_problem "$_CYCLE_UNTIL_OP" "$_CYCLE_UNTIL_VALUE")"
427	        if [[ -n "$_u_pp" ]]; then
428	            error "cycle '$cycle_id': until (field '$_CYCLE_UNTIL_FIELD'): $_u_pp"
429	            _cycle_emit "cycle.config.invalid" "reason=until_op_invalid" \
430	                "value=$_CYCLE_UNTIL_OP"
431	            return 1
432	        fi
433	        # until.stage must be in cycle.stages
434	        local _us_ok=0 s
435	        for s in "${_CYCLE_STAGES[@]}"; do
436	            [[ "$s" == "$_CYCLE_UNTIL_STAGE" ]] && _us_ok=1 && break
437	        done
438	        if [[ $_us_ok -ne 1 ]]; then
439	            error "cycle '$cycle_id': until.stage '$_CYCLE_UNTIL_STAGE' is not in cycle stages (${_CYCLE_STAGES[*]})"
440	            _cycle_emit "cycle.config.invalid" "reason=until_stage_outside_cycle" \
441	                "value=$_CYCLE_UNTIL_STAGE"
442	            return 1
443	        fi
444	    fi
445	
446	    local pw="${!pw_var:-}"; [[ -n "$pw" && "$pw" =~ ^[0-9]+$ ]] && _CYCLE_PLATEAU_WINDOW="$pw"
447	    local dw="${!dw_var:-}"; [[ -n "$dw" && "$dw" =~ ^[0-9]+$ ]] && _CYCLE_DIVERGENCE_WINDOW="$dw"
448	    local vpw_var="_TPL_CYCLE_VELOCITY_PLATEAU_W_${safe}"
449	    local vpw="${!vpw_var:-}"; [[ -n "$vpw" && "$vpw" =~ ^[0-9]+$ ]] && _CYCLE_VELOCITY_PLATEAU_WINDOW="$vpw"
450	
451	    return 0
452	}

454	# ─── _cycle_record_iter_outcome ──────────────────────────────────────────────
455	# Appends a JSONL row to the per-cycle history file. Schema:
456	#   {"n":N,"verdict":..,"status":..,"failure_count":N,"ts":"..."}
457	# Failure to write is HIGH severity — emit cycle.history.lost and propagate.
458	_cycle_record_iter_outcome() {
459	    local history_file="$1" n="$2" verdict="$3" status="$4" failure_count="$5"
460	    local ts; TZ=UTC0 printf -v ts '%(%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ)T' -1
461	    local line
462	    line="$(jq -nc \
463	        --argjson n "$n" \
464	        --arg verdict "$verdict" \
465	        --arg status "$status" \
466	        --argjson fc "$failure_count" \
467	        --arg ts "$ts" \
468	        '{n:$n, verdict:$verdict, status:$status, failure_count:$fc, ts:$ts}' \
469	        2>/dev/null)" || {
470	        _cycle_emit "cycle.history.lost" "iter=$n" "reason=jq_render_failed"
471	        return 1
472	    }
473	    local _hd; zb_dirname_v _hd "$history_file"
474	    [[ -d "$_hd" ]] || mkdir -p "$_hd" 2>/dev/null || true
475	    if ! printf '%s\n' "$line" >> "$history_file" 2>/dev/null; then
476	        _cycle_emit "cycle.history.lost" "iter=$n" "reason=append_failed" \
477	            "history_file=$history_file"
478	        return 1
479	    fi
480	    return 0
481	}

483	# _cycle_op_match <where> <op> <actual> <expected> — one condition, by ADR-027
484	# §5's eight ops: rc 0 match, 1 no match. A condition that cannot be evaluated
485	# (an op off the list, a number op on a word, a malformed pattern) is no match
486	# and sets _CYCLE_OP_ERROR, said in the log and as an event — never a silent
487	# no-match (#1760). The op and value are checked by the loader's own rule.
488	_cycle_op_match() {
489	    local where="$1" op="$2" actual="$3" expected="$4"
490	    _CYCLE_OP_ERROR="$(_tpl_predicate_problem "$op" "$expected")"
491	    if [[ -z "$_CYCLE_OP_ERROR" ]]; then
492	        case "$op" in
493	            gt|gte|lt|lte)
494	                [[ "$actual" =~ ^-?[0-9]+$ ]] \
495	                    || _CYCLE_OP_ERROR="op '$op' needs a whole number; the $where field is '$actual'" ;;
496	        esac
497	    fi
498	    if [[ -n "$_CYCLE_OP_ERROR" ]]; then
499	        error "cycle $where: $_CYCLE_OP_ERROR"
500	        _cycle_emit "cycle.config.invalid" "reason=predicate_error" "where=$where" "op=$op" "detail=$_CYCLE_OP_ERROR"
501	        return 1
502	    fi
503	    case "$op" in
504	        eq)       [[ "$actual" == "$expected" ]] ;;
505	        neq)      [[ "$actual" != "$expected" ]] ;;
506	        gt)       (( actual >  expected )) ;;
507	        gte)      (( actual >= expected )) ;;
508	        lt)       (( actual <  expected )) ;;
509	        lte)      (( actual <= expected )) ;;
510	        contains) [[ "$actual" == *"$expected"* ]] ;;
511	        matches)  [[ "$actual" =~ $expected ]] ;;
512	    esac
513	}
514	
515	# ─── _cycle_eval_one_condition <blob> <stage> <field> <op> <expected> ─────────
516	# Evaluate a single predicate against the blob. Returns 0 (match) or 1 (no match).
517	# Emits cycle.iteration.verdict_missing when the field is absent.
518	# Does NOT stash the predicate (caller decides which one to stash for the banner).
519	_cycle_eval_one_condition() {
520	    local blob="$1" stage="$2" field="$3" op="$4" expected="$5"
521	    local actual
522	    actual="$(jq -r --arg s "$stage" --arg f "$field" \
523	        '.[$s][$f] // empty' <<< "$blob" 2>/dev/null || true)"
524	    if [[ -z "$actual" || "$actual" == "null" ]]; then
525	        _cycle_emit "cycle.iteration.verdict_missing" \
526	            "iter=$_CYCLE_TRAP_ITER" "stage=$stage" "field=$field"
527	        _cycle_emit_predicate "exit_when" "$stage" "$field" "$op" "$expected" "" "false"
528	        return 1
529	    fi
530	    local _match="false"
531	    local _rc=1
532	    _cycle_op_match exit_when "$op" "$actual" "$expected"; _rc=$?
533	    [[ $_rc -eq 0 ]] && _match="true"
534	    _cycle_emit_predicate "exit_when" "$stage" "$field" "$op" "$expected" "$actual" "$_match"
535	    return $_rc
536	}

538	# ─── _cycle_check_until <stage_verdicts_jsonblob> ────────────────────────────
539	# Returns 0 if predicate satisfied (converged), 1 otherwise.
540	# Stage-verdicts blob is JSON: {"<stage>":{"verdict":"pass","status":"complete"}}.
541	# Field-missing → 1 (NEVER falsely converge). Emits verdict_missing once.
542	# #1284 (ADR-047): when _CYCLE_EXIT_COMBINATOR is set, evaluates N conditions
543	# with all/any logic. Single-condition path is BYTE-IDENTICAL to prior behavior.
544	_cycle_check_until() {
545	    local blob="$1"
546	
547	    # #1284: multi-condition path.
548	    if [[ -n "${_CYCLE_EXIT_COMBINATOR:-}" && ${#_CYCLE_EXIT_CONDITIONS[@]} -gt 0 ]]; then
549	        # all: start converged, fail on first miss. any: start diverged, pass on first hit.
550	        local _ew_overall_rc _ew_cond _ew_s _ew_f _ew_o _ew_v _ew_rc _ew_rest
551	        local _ew_last_stage="" _ew_last_field="" _ew_last_op="" _ew_last_expected="" _ew_last_match="false"
552	        [[ "$_CYCLE_EXIT_COMBINATOR" == "all" ]] && _ew_overall_rc=0 || _ew_overall_rc=1
553	        # Save errexit state before loop — toggling set -e/+e per-iteration leaks the
554	        # restored set -e to our caller when we return rc=1, triggering their errexit.
555	        local _ew_had_e=0; [[ "$-" == *e* ]] && _ew_had_e=1; set +e
556	        for _ew_cond in "${_CYCLE_EXIT_CONDITIONS[@]}"; do
557	            _ew_s="${_ew_cond%%|*}"; _ew_rest="${_ew_cond#*|}"
558	            _ew_f="${_ew_rest%%|*}"; _ew_rest="${_ew_rest#*|}"
559	            _ew_o="${_ew_rest%%|*}"; _ew_v="${_ew_rest#*|}"
560	            _cycle_eval_one_condition "$blob" "$_ew_s" "$_ew_f" "$_ew_o" "$_ew_v"; _ew_rc=$?
561	            _ew_last_stage="$_ew_s"; _ew_last_field="$_ew_f"
562	            _ew_last_op="$_ew_o"; _ew_last_expected="$_ew_v"
563	            if [[ "$_ew_rc" -eq 0 ]]; then
564	                _ew_last_match="true"
565	                [[ "$_CYCLE_EXIT_COMBINATOR" == "any" ]] && { _ew_overall_rc=0; break; }
566	            else
567	                _ew_last_match="false"
568	                [[ "$_CYCLE_EXIT_COMBINATOR" == "all" ]] && { _ew_overall_rc=1; break; }
569	            fi
570	        done
571	        [[ $_ew_had_e -eq 1 ]] && set -e
572	        local _ew_actual
573	        _ew_actual="$(jq -r --arg s "$_ew_last_stage" --arg f "$_ew_last_field" \
574	            '.[$s][$f] // empty' <<< "$blob" 2>/dev/null || true)"
575	        _cycle_stash_predicate "exit_when" "$_ew_last_stage" "$_ew_last_field" \
576	            "$_ew_last_op" "$_ew_last_expected" "$_ew_actual" "$_ew_last_match"
577	        return $_ew_overall_rc
578	    fi
579	
580	    # Single-condition path — byte-identical to pre-#1284 behavior.
581	    local stage="$_CYCLE_UNTIL_STAGE"
582	    local field="$_CYCLE_UNTIL_FIELD"
583	    local op="$_CYCLE_UNTIL_OP"
584	    local expected="$_CYCLE_UNTIL_VALUE"
585	    local actual
586	    actual="$(jq -r --arg s "$stage" --arg f "$field" \
587	        '.[$s][$f] // empty' <<< "$blob" 2>/dev/null || true)"
588	    if [[ -z "$actual" || "$actual" == "null" ]]; then
589	        _cycle_emit "cycle.iteration.verdict_missing" \
590	            "iter=$_CYCLE_TRAP_ITER" "stage=$stage" "field=$field"
591	        _cycle_emit_predicate "exit_when" "$stage" "$field" "$op" "$expected" "" "false"
592	        # #833: stash for the cycle OUTPUT banner (missing → empty actual).
593	        _cycle_stash_predicate "exit_when" "$stage" "$field" "$op" "$expected" "" "false"
594	        return 1
595	    fi
596	    local _match="false"
597	    local _rc=1
598	    _cycle_op_match until "$op" "$actual" "$expected"; _rc=$?
599	    [[ $_rc -eq 0 ]] && _match="true"
600	    _cycle_emit_predicate "exit_when" "$stage" "$field" "$op" "$expected" "$actual" "$_match"
601	    # #833: stash the just-evaluated predicate so _cycle_render_predicate_result
602	    # can restate it on the cycle OUTPUT banner.
603	    _cycle_stash_predicate "exit_when" "$stage" "$field" "$op" "$expected" "$actual" "$_match"
604	    return $_rc
605	}

608	# The loop's summary of what happened this round: every member, its outcome and
609	# its one-line reason, in artifacts/<loop>-summary.md. Rewritten each round, so
610	# it always says what the latest round did. Fail-open.
611	_cycle_write_round_summary() {

617	        body+="${line:-- $m: missing}"$'\n'

652	# _cycle_render_summaries_digest <state_dir> (#2124) — how many stage summaries
653	# the next stage's Previous work carries, and how many of those stages failed.
654	_cycle_render_summaries_digest() {

672	# ─── _cycle_read_progress <state_dir> (#1243) ────────────────────────────────
673	# Code-change PROGRESS axis for the cycle health score: the changes the members
674	# of ONE iteration reported (#2189 — the verdicts blob, not a stage's file),
675	# echoed as "<files_changed> <lines_added> <lines_removed>". No report, or a
676	# cycle whose members change nothing, reads as "0 0 0" (→ "no progress").
677	_cycle_read_progress() {
678	    local blob="${1:-}"
679	    [[ -n "$blob" ]] || blob='{}'
680	    local out
681	    out="$(jq -r '
682	        [ .[]? | (.report.changes // empty) ] as $cs
683	        | ([ $cs[] | (.files // [])[] ] | unique | length) as $f
684	        | ([ $cs[] | (.added // 0) ] | add // 0) as $a
685	        | ([ $cs[] | (.removed // 0) ] | add // 0) as $r
686	        | "\($f) \($a) \($r)"' <<< "$blob" 2>/dev/null || true)"
687	    local files add del
688	    read -r files add del <<< "$out"
689	    [[ "$files" =~ ^[0-9]+$ ]] || files=0
690	    [[ "$add"   =~ ^[0-9]+$ ]] || add=0
691	    [[ "$del"   =~ ^[0-9]+$ ]] || del=0
692	    printf '%s %s %s' "$files" "$add" "$del"
693	    return 0
694	}

696	# ─── _cycle_commit_member (#2189) ────────────────────────────────────────────
697	# The cycle member whose manifest declares capabilities.produces_commits — found
698	# by declaration (ADR-047 §4), never by the stage name `build`. Empty if none.
699	_cycle_commit_member() {

701	    _manifest_graph_ensure_yaml_get 2>/dev/null || true
702	    for _m in "${_CYCLE_STAGES[@]}"; do
703	        _mf="$(manifest_graph_resolve_member "$_root" "$_m" 2>/dev/null)" || continue
704	        if [[ "$(yaml_get "$_mf" "capabilities.produces_commits" 2>/dev/null || true)" == "true" ]]; then
705	            printf '%s' "$_m"; return 0
706	        fi
707	    done
708	    return 0
709	}

712	# Whether any member of the iteration reported a test count, and whether any such
713	# member reported failures (a count > 0, or its own verdict fail). Decided from
714	# the reports — no member named `test`, no test-results.json read by path.
715	_cycle_tests_reported() {

732	# ─── _cycle_render_predicate_result <iter> [state_dir] (#833, #1241, #1243) ───
733	# Builds the cycle OUTPUT-banner body from the last-stashed predicate eval:
734	#   line1: <kind> stage=<s> field=<f> op=<op> value=<v> → MATCHED|NOT MATCHED (got=<actual>)
735	#   line2 (#1243): multi-axis health score, human-readable, calculation shown.
736	#   line3 (#1241, NOT MATCHED only): failed gates: <list>[ — <reason>]
737	# #1243: the old single-axis `velocity=0-fc` was misleading — an iteration that
738	# applied ZERO code read only as "more defects". The health line now combines
739	# two axes into one total with the arithmetic visible:
740	#   code-change PROGRESS (lines_added+lines_removed this iter) − DEFECTS (fc)
741	#     → SCORE. A zero-diff iter explicitly reads "no progress" (distinct from a
742	#   regression).
743	# #1241: the optional <state_dir> lets the banner name what blocked (not just
744	# "NOT MATCHED (got=fail)"); omitted → no failed-gates line. Pure/read-only; no errexit hazard.
745	_cycle_render_predicate_result() {
746	    local iter="$1"
747	    local state_dir="${2:-}"
748	    local kind="${_CYCLE_LAST_PREDICATE_KIND:-exit_when}"
749	    local stage="${_CYCLE_LAST_PREDICATE_STAGE:-}"
750	    local field="${_CYCLE_LAST_PREDICATE_FIELD:-}"
751	    local op="${_CYCLE_LAST_PREDICATE_OP:-}"
752	    local expected="${_CYCLE_LAST_PREDICATE_EXPECTED:-}"
753	    local actual="${_CYCLE_LAST_PREDICATE_ACTUAL:-}"
754	    local match="${_CYCLE_LAST_PREDICATE_MATCH:-false}"
755	    local fc="${_CYCLE_LAST_FAILURE_COUNT:-0}"

757	    local matched_str="NOT MATCHED (got=${actual})"

759	
760	    local files add del
761	    read -r files add del <<< "$(_cycle_read_progress "${_CYCLE_LAST_VERDICTS_BLOB:-}")"

764	    local health_line

767	        health_line="$(printf 'health: progress=0 (no progress) - defects=%s → score=%s' "$fc" "$score")"

785	            printf '\nfailed gates: %s' "$_failed"
