51	_ARTIFACT_PERSIST_LAST_STATUS=""
52	# #1921: WHERE a restore came from — "local" (refs/heads) or "remote"
53	# (refs/remotes/origin); empty for non-restore operations. "The branch exists"
54	# and "this run fetched it from origin" are different facts, and only the second
55	# answers whether a CI run started WARM. Without this the question can only be
56	# inferred from log lines.
57	_ARTIFACT_PERSIST_LAST_SOURCE=""
58	_ARTIFACT_PERSIST_LAST_REASON=""
59	_ARTIFACT_PERSIST_LAST_SKIPPED=0

70	# ─── _artifact_persist_find_secret <artifacts_dir> (#2187) ───────────────────
71	# Echo "<relpath>:<kind>" for the first text artifact that looks like it carries
72	# a credential, rc 0; rc 1 when none does. The ONE scan every push path runs —
73	# it lived only in the persist stage, and #2187's stage-end push must not be a
74	# way around it. Patterns: scripts/lib/secret-patterns.sh.
75	_artifact_persist_find_secret() {
76	    local art_dir="$1" f rel kind
77	    [[ -d "$art_dir" ]] || return 1
78	    if ! declare -F zbuild_scan_secret_content >/dev/null 2>&1 \
79	        || ! declare -F zbuild_secret_candidate_files >/dev/null 2>&1; then
80	        # shellcheck source=../../scripts/lib/secret-patterns.sh
81	        source "$(cd "${BASH_SOURCE[0]%/*}" 2>/dev/null || true; cd ../../scripts/lib 2>/dev/null && pwd)/secret-patterns.sh" 2>/dev/null || {
82	            # No scanner, no proof the content is clean: refuse, never pass.
83	            printf '%s:scan_unavailable' "${art_dir##*/}"
84	            return 0
85	        }
86	    fi
87	    local repo="${2:-$PWD}" base="" content
88	    # Only a text file a pattern matches can be flagged: find those with two
89	    # greps over the dir and read just them, so a clean dir costs no more.
90	    # No trailing slash, so grep and find name each file the same way.
91	    [[ "$art_dir" == "/" ]] || art_dir="${art_dir%/}"
92	    local -A cand=()
93	    while IFS= read -r -d '' f; do cand["$f"]=1; done < <(zbuild_secret_candidate_files "$art_dir")
94	    [[ ${#cand[@]} -gt 0 ]] || return 1
95	    # Walked in find order, as before, so the first flagged file is the same.
96	    while IFS= read -r -d '' f; do
97	        [[ -n "${cand["$f"]:-}" ]] || continue
98	        content="$(cat "$f" 2>/dev/null)"
99	        kind="$(zbuild_scan_secret_content "$content")" || continue
100	        [[ -n "$base" ]] || base="$(_artifact_persist_scan_base "$repo")"
101	        _artifact_persist_has_new_secret_line "$content" "$repo" "$base" || continue
102	        rel="${f#"$art_dir"/}"
103	        printf '%s:%s' "$rel" "$kind"
104	        return 0
105	    done < <(find "$art_dir" -type f -print0 2>/dev/null)
106	    return 1
107	}

109	# The merge-base the secret-scan gate diffs against, or "-" when none resolves.
110	# "-" (not empty) so the caller resolves it once per scan, not once per file.
111	_artifact_persist_scan_base() {
112	    if ! declare -F zbuild_resolve_merge_base >/dev/null 2>&1; then
113	        # shellcheck source=../../scripts/lib/merge-base.sh
114	        source "$(cd "${BASH_SOURCE[0]%/*}" 2>/dev/null || true; cd ../../scripts/lib 2>/dev/null && pwd)/merge-base.sh" 2>/dev/null || true
115	    fi
116	    local b=""
117	    declare -F zbuild_resolve_merge_base >/dev/null 2>&1 && b="$(zbuild_resolve_merge_base "$1")"
118	    printf '%s' "${b:--}"
119	}

121	# rc 0 when <content> has a credential-shaped line the RUN introduced — the same
122	# scope as the secret-scan gate, which judges added lines only (#1835's run was
123	# refused over a test line on main since #1114). A line is excused when it
124	# carries the allow pragma or already exists verbatim at the merge-base. With no
125	# merge-base nothing can be excused: fail closed.
126	_artifact_persist_has_new_secret_line() {
127	    local content="$1" repo="$2" base="$3" line needle
128	    while IFS= read -r line; do
129	        [[ -z "$line" ]] && continue
130	        zbuild_secret_line_allowlisted "$line" && continue
131	        [[ "$base" == "-" ]] && return 0
132	        # A diff's context marker is not part of the source line; a '+' line is
133	        # added by definition and will not be found at the base.
134	        needle="${line#[+ -]}"
135	        needle="${needle#"${needle%%[![:space:]]*}"}"
136	        git -C "$repo" grep -qF -e "$needle" "$base" -- 2>/dev/null || return 0
137	    done < <(zbuild_secret_matching_lines "$content")
138	    return 1
139	}

141	# ─── _artifact_persist_has_identity <issue> [goal] ───────────────────────────
142	# rc=0 when this run has an identity to persist UNDER — an issue number, or a
143	# goal (#1931). Replaces the `issue > 0` idiom, which predates goal identity and
144	# silently excluded every --goal run from the durable store.
145	#
146	# The guard must be the IDENTITY, not the issue number. Guarding on `issue > 0`
147	# and then deriving the branch means the derivation never runs for a goal run,
148	# so `zbuild/state/goal-<hash>` is computed correctly and never used — which is
149	# exactly the gap review found: the branch NAME was right and nothing pushed to
150	# it.
151	_artifact_persist_has_identity() {
152	    local issue="${1:-0}" goal="${2:-${ZBUILD_GOAL:-}}"
153	    [[ "$issue" =~ ^[0-9]+$ && "$issue" -gt 0 ]] && return 0
154	    [[ -n "${goal//[[:space:]]/}" ]] && declare -F zbuild_run_key >/dev/null 2>&1
155	}

157	# ─── _artifact_persist_branch <issue> ───────────────────────────────────────
158	# The state branch name for an issue. Sibling to the work branch; never merged.
159	# #1931: takes the goal text as an optional second argument so a `--goal` run
160	# gets its own durable branch instead of sharing `issue-0` with every other one.
161	# Callers that pass only an issue are unchanged.
162	_artifact_persist_branch() { local _apb; _artifact_persist_branch_v _apb "$@"; printf '%s' "$_apb"; }
163	# _artifact_persist_branch_v <var> [issue] [goal] — the same into <var>. A run
164	# snapshots after every stage, so a goal's key (a hash) is worked out once a
165	# shell (ADR-065 §5, round 9).
166	declare -gA _AP_BRANCH_MEMO=()
167	_artifact_persist_branch_v() {
168	    local -n _apbo="$1"
169	    local issue="${2:-0}" goal="${3:-${ZBUILD_GOAL:-}}"
170	    if [[ "$issue" =~ ^[0-9]+$ && "$issue" -gt 0 ]]; then
171	        _apbo="zbuild/state/issue-$issue"
172	        return 0
173	    fi
174	    local mk="$issue"$'\034'"$goal"
175	    if [[ -n "${_AP_BRANCH_MEMO[$mk]+x}" ]]; then _apbo="${_AP_BRANCH_MEMO[$mk]}"; return 0; fi
176	    local key=""
177	    if declare -F zbuild_run_key >/dev/null 2>&1; then
178	        key="$(zbuild_run_key "$issue" "$goal" 2>/dev/null || true)"
179	    fi
180	    if [[ -n "$key" ]]; then
181	        _apbo="zbuild/state/$key"
182	    else
183	        # Unchanged fallback: no issue and no goal is no identity.
184	        _apbo="zbuild/state/issue-$issue"
185	    fi
186	    _AP_BRANCH_MEMO[$mk]="$_apbo"
187	}
188	# _artifact_persist_tmp_name_v <var> <prefix> — a path in the engine's temp dir
189	# that does not exist yet, as `mktemp -u` names one, without starting it.
190	_artifact_persist_tmp_name_v() {
191	    local -n _aptn="$1"
192	    local _aptd _apti
193	    zbuild_engine_tmpdir_v _aptd
194	    for (( _apti = 0; _apti < 10; _apti++ )); do
195	        _aptn="$_aptd/$2.$BASHPID.$RANDOM$RANDOM"
196	        [[ -e "$_aptn" ]] || return 0
197	    done
198	    _aptn=""; return 1

200	# ─── _artifact_persist_git_dir <repo_root> ───────────────────────────────────
201	# Resolve the git dir to use for plumbing. NOT "$repo_root/.git": in a linked
202	# worktree that path is a FILE (`gitdir: …/.git/worktrees/<name>`), and while git
203	# does follow the pointer, it resolves to the PER-WORKTREE git dir. Objects are
204	# shared, so blobs and trees are safe — but refs are not: `update-ref
205	# refs/heads/zbuild/state/issue-N` would land in that worktree's ref view rather
206	# than the shared store, so the next run would not find the state branch.
207	# --git-common-dir returns the shared dir for both a main tree and a worktree.
208	_artifact_persist_git_dir() { local _apgd; _artifact_persist_git_dir_v _apgd "${1:-}"; printf '%s' "$_apgd"; }
209	# _artifact_persist_git_dir_v <var> <repo_root> — the same into <var>, asked of
210	# git once per repo per shell: the shared git dir does not move (ADR-065 §5).
211	declare -gA _AP_GIT_DIR_MEMO=()
212	_artifact_persist_git_dir_v() {
213	    local -n _apgv="$1"
214	    local repo_root="${2:-}" d
215	    if [[ -n "${_AP_GIT_DIR_MEMO[$repo_root]:-}" ]]; then _apgv="${_AP_GIT_DIR_MEMO[$repo_root]}"; return 0; fi
216	    if ! d="$(git -C "$repo_root" rev-parse --git-common-dir 2>/dev/null)"; then
217	        _apgv="$repo_root/.git"; return 0   # not remembered: a failure may pass
218	    fi
219	    # --git-common-dir may be relative to repo_root (commonly ".git").
220	    case "$d" in
221	        /*) _apgv="$d" ;;
222	        *)  _apgv="$repo_root/$d" ;;
223	    esac
224	    _AP_GIT_DIR_MEMO[$repo_root]="$_apgv"
225	}

227	# ─── _artifact_persist_stage_batch <git_dir> <index> (#2249) ─────────────────
228	# Stage _abs[] (paths) / _rel[] (names in the tree) into <index> in two git
229	# calls. The two arrays are NOT parameters: they are the caller's locals, read
230	# through bash dynamic scope, so only _artifact_persist_snapshot (which fills
231	# them) may call this. A tab inside a path is safe: --index-info takes the path
232	# as everything after the first tab (artifact-persist-batch-test B4).
233	# rc 1 — nothing trusted — when either call fails, a path holds a newline
234	# (stdin is line-delimited), or the blob count does not match.
235	_artifact_persist_stage_batch() {
236	    local gd="$1" idx="$2" paths="" blobs info="" i b
237	    (( ${#_abs[@]} > 0 )) || return 1
238	    for (( i = 0; i < ${#_abs[@]}; i++ )); do
239	        [[ "${_abs[$i]}" == *$'\n'* || "${_rel[$i]}" == *$'\n'* ]] && return 1
240	        paths+="${_abs[$i]}"$'\n'
241	    done
242	    blobs="$(GIT_DIR="$gd" git hash-object -w --stdin-paths 2>/dev/null <<< "${paths%$'\n'}")" || return 1
243	    local -a _b=()
244	    mapfile -t _b <<< "$blobs"
245	    (( ${#_b[@]} == ${#_abs[@]} )) || return 1
246	    for (( i = 0; i < ${#_b[@]}; i++ )); do
247	        b="${_b[$i]}"
248	        [[ "$b" =~ ^[0-9a-f]{40,64}$ ]] || return 1
249	        info+="100644 $b"$'\t'"${_rel[$i]}"$'\n'
250	    done
251	    GIT_INDEX_FILE="$idx" GIT_DIR="$gd" git update-index --index-info 2>/dev/null <<< "${info%$'\n'}"
252	}

254	# ─── _artifact_persist_snapshot <state_dir> <issue> [repo_root] ─────────────
255	# Commit the current artifact area onto the state branch WITHOUT touching the
256	# working tree or the real index (uses a throwaway GIT_INDEX_FILE + plumbing).
257	# Snapshots state/artifacts/** plus a few top-level state docs if present.
258	# Returns 0 on success (or clean no-op when there is nothing to snapshot), 1 on
259	# any git failure. Never disturbs the caller's checkout.
260	_artifact_persist_snapshot() {
261	    _artifact_persist_reset_status
262	    local state_dir="$1" issue="${2:-0}" repo_root="${3:-$(git rev-parse --show-toplevel 2>/dev/null)}"
263	    # #1921: "amend" replaces the branch tip instead of committing on top of it.
264	    # persist must snapshot twice — the first snapshot cannot contain the result
265	    # file that describes it — and a second commit whose only delta is a status
266	    # file is the commit spam ADR-050 §4 rules out. Callers pass this ONLY when
267	    # they created the current tip themselves this invocation; amending a tip
268	    # written by someone else would discard a legitimate boundary snapshot.
269	    local mode="${4:-}"
270	    # Resolve the SHARED git dir before the guard uses it. The guard previously
271	    # tested `-d "$repo_root/.git"`, which is FALSE in a linked worktree (.git is
272	    # a file there), so persistence would silently no-op inside a worktree.
273	    local _gd=""
274	    [[ -n "$repo_root" ]] && _artifact_persist_git_dir_v _gd "$repo_root"
275	    # #1878: this is NOT "nothing to do" — it means we could not resolve a repo to
276	    # persist INTO, which is a real failure the caller must be able to see. It
277	    # used to `return 0`, which the runner reported as a successful snapshot.
278	    if [[ -z "$repo_root" || ! -d "$_gd" ]]; then
279	        _ARTIFACT_PERSIST_LAST_STATUS="failed"
280	        _ARTIFACT_PERSIST_LAST_REASON="unresolvable repo: repo_root=[${repo_root:-<empty>}] git_dir=[${_gd:-<empty>}] cwd=[$PWD]"
281	        return 1
282	    fi
283	    local art_dir="$state_dir/artifacts"
284	    if [[ ! -d "$art_dir" ]]; then
285	        _ARTIFACT_PERSIST_LAST_STATUS="empty"
286	        _ARTIFACT_PERSIST_LAST_REASON="no artifact dir at $art_dir"
287	        return 0
288	    fi
289	
290	    local branch; _artifact_persist_branch_v branch "$issue"
291	    # A NON-existent path: git initializes a fresh index there. A pre-created
292	    # empty file (plain mktemp) is rejected as "index file smaller than expected".
293	    local tmp_index
294	    if ! _artifact_persist_tmp_name_v tmp_index zbuild-persist-idx; then
295	        _ARTIFACT_PERSIST_LAST_STATUS="failed"
296	        _ARTIFACT_PERSIST_LAST_REASON="no free name for the throwaway index (TMPDIR=${TMPDIR:-/tmp})"
297	        return 1
298	    fi
299	
300	    # Build a tree from the artifact files under a stable prefix (artifacts/…),
301	    # plus a couple of top-level state docs, in a throwaway index.
302	    #
303	    # #1878: SKIP a file we cannot stage, do not abort the snapshot. This loop
304	    # used to `break` on the first failure, discarding every artifact already
305	    # staged — while the `extra` loop below has always skipped-and-continued. A
306	    # file that vanished mid-scan (the artifact area has live writers) or is
307	    # unreadable must cost us that one file, not the whole snapshot.
308	    local added=0 skipped=0 f rel blob first_skip="" n
309	    local -a _abs=() _rel=()
310	    while IFS= read -r -d '' f; do
311	        _abs+=("$f"); _rel+=("artifacts/${f#"$art_dir"/}")
312	    done < <(find "$art_dir" -type f -print0 2>/dev/null)
313	    # Include a handful of top-level state docs when present (scope manifest etc.).
314	    local extra
315	    for extra in scope-manifest.md intake.md; do
316	        [[ -f "$state_dir/$extra" ]] || continue
317	        _abs+=("$state_dir/$extra"); _rel+=("$extra")
318	    done
319	
320	    # #2249: two git calls for the whole set — `hash-object --stdin-paths` and
321	    # `update-index --index-info` — instead of two per file (a run snapshots
322	    # after every stage, over hundreds of files). Any failure in the batch (an
323	    # unreadable file aborts hash-object) falls back to the per-file loop below,
324	    # so #1878's rule holds: a file we cannot stage costs only that file.
325	    if _artifact_persist_stage_batch "$_gd" "$tmp_index"; then
326	        added=${#_abs[@]}
327	    else
328	        rm -f "$tmp_index"
329	        for (( n = 0; n < ${#_abs[@]}; n++ )); do
330	            f="${_abs[$n]}"; rel="${_rel[$n]}"
331	            if ! blob="$(GIT_DIR="$_gd" git hash-object -w "$f" 2>/dev/null)"; then
332	                skipped=$((skipped + 1)); [[ -z "$first_skip" ]] && first_skip="$rel (hash-object)"
333	                continue
334	            fi
335	            # #1878: a refused entry is a skip, never counted as staged.
336	            if ! GIT_INDEX_FILE="$tmp_index" GIT_DIR="$_gd" \
337	                    git update-index --add --cacheinfo "100644,$blob,$rel" 2>/dev/null; then
338	                skipped=$((skipped + 1)); [[ -z "$first_skip" ]] && first_skip="$rel (update-index)"
339	                continue
340	            fi
341	            added=$((added + 1))
342	        done
343	    fi
344	
345	    _ARTIFACT_PERSIST_LAST_SKIPPED="$skipped"
346	
347	    # Nothing staged at all. If files were SKIPPED that is a failure (we had work
348	    # and lost it); if there were simply no files, it is an honest empty.
349	    if [[ "$added" -eq 0 ]]; then
350	        rm -f "$tmp_index"
351	        if [[ "$skipped" -gt 0 ]]; then
352	            _ARTIFACT_PERSIST_LAST_STATUS="failed"
353	            _ARTIFACT_PERSIST_LAST_REASON="all $skipped file(s) unstageable, first: $first_skip"
354	            return 1
355	        fi
356	        _ARTIFACT_PERSIST_LAST_STATUS="empty"
357	        _ARTIFACT_PERSIST_LAST_REASON="no files under $art_dir"
358	        return 0
359	    fi
360	
361	    # #1878: capture stderr from the terminal ops. They used to be 2>/dev/null
362	    # followed by a bare `return 1`, so a failure named itself and destroyed its
363	    # own explanation — the #1631 anti-pattern, and the reason this defect went
364	    # undiagnosed for the life of the feature.
365	    local tree parent commit err
366	    if ! tree="$(GIT_INDEX_FILE="$tmp_index" GIT_DIR="$_gd" git write-tree 2>"$tmp_index.err")"; then
367	        err="$(cat "$tmp_index.err" 2>/dev/null | tr '\n' ' ')"
368	        rm -f "$tmp_index" "$tmp_index.err"
369	        _ARTIFACT_PERSIST_LAST_STATUS="failed"
370	        _ARTIFACT_PERSIST_LAST_REASON="git write-tree failed: ${err:-<no stderr>} (git_dir=$_gd)"
371	        return 1
372	    fi
373	    rm -f "$tmp_index" "$tmp_index.err"
374	
375	    local tip; tip="$(GIT_DIR="$_gd" git rev-parse -q --verify "refs/heads/$branch" 2>/dev/null || true)"
376	
377	    # Unchanged is judged against the TIP in both modes: it asks "does the branch
378	    # already say this?", which amending does not change.
379	    if [[ -n "$tip" ]]; then
380	        local tip_tree; tip_tree="$(GIT_DIR="$_gd" git rev-parse -q --verify "$tip^{tree}" 2>/dev/null || true)"
381	        if [[ "$tip_tree" == "$tree" ]]; then
382	            _ARTIFACT_PERSIST_LAST_STATUS="unchanged"
383	            _ARTIFACT_PERSIST_LAST_REASON="tree identical to $branch tip"
384	            return 0
385	        fi
386	    fi
387	
388	    if [[ "$mode" == "amend" && -n "$tip" ]]; then
389	        # Parent is the tip's parent, so the new commit REPLACES the tip. Empty
390	        # when the tip is a root commit, which correctly yields a new root.
391	        parent="$(GIT_DIR="$_gd" git rev-parse -q --verify "${tip}^" 2>/dev/null || true)"
392	    else
393	        parent="$tip"
394	    fi
395	
396	    local msg="zbuild: persist artifacts for #$issue [skip ci]"
397	    # PR #1880 review: guard the mktemp. An unguarded one leaves _ct_err empty,
398	    # `2>""` then fails to open, and commit-tree fails for the WRONG reason with
399	    # no captured stderr — a silent failure inside the code whose whole purpose is
400	    # to stop silent failures. /dev/null is the honest fallback: we lose the
401	    # stderr detail but still report the real git failure.
402	    local _ct_err; _artifact_persist_tmp_name_v _ct_err zbuild-persist-err || _ct_err="/dev/null"
403	    if [[ -n "$parent" ]]; then
404	        commit="$(GIT_DIR="$_gd" git commit-tree "$tree" -p "$parent" -m "$msg" 2>"$_ct_err")" || commit=""
405	    else
406	        commit="$(GIT_DIR="$_gd" git commit-tree "$tree" -m "$msg" 2>"$_ct_err")" || commit=""
407	    fi
408	    if [[ -z "$commit" ]]; then
409	        err="$(cat "$_ct_err" 2>/dev/null | tr '\n' ' ')"
410	        rm -f "$_ct_err"
411	        _ARTIFACT_PERSIST_LAST_STATUS="failed"
412	        # A missing committer identity lands here — the most likely cause on a
413	        # fresh runner, and previously indistinguishable from every other failure.
414	        _ARTIFACT_PERSIST_LAST_REASON="git commit-tree failed: ${err:-<no stderr>} (git_dir=$_gd)"
415	        return 1
416	    fi
417	    rm -f "$_ct_err"
418	
419	    # PR #1880 review: guarded (see the _ct_err note above).
420	    local _ur_err; _artifact_persist_tmp_name_v _ur_err zbuild-persist-err || _ur_err="/dev/null"
421	    if ! GIT_DIR="$_gd" git update-ref "refs/heads/$branch" "$commit" 2>"$_ur_err"; then
422	        err="$(cat "$_ur_err" 2>/dev/null | tr '\n' ' ')"
423	        rm -f "$_ur_err"
424	        _ARTIFACT_PERSIST_LAST_STATUS="failed"
425	        _ARTIFACT_PERSIST_LAST_REASON="git update-ref $branch failed: ${err:-<no stderr>} (git_dir=$_gd)"
426	        return 1
427	    fi
428	    rm -f "$_ur_err"
429	
430	    _ARTIFACT_PERSIST_LAST_STATUS="saved"
431	    _ARTIFACT_PERSIST_LAST_REASON="staged $added file(s), skipped $skipped"
432	    return 0
433	}
434	
435	# ─── _artifact_persist_adopt_remote <issue> [repo_root] (#1921) ─────────────
436	# Point the LOCAL `refs/heads/<branch>` at the fetched remote-tracking ref, but
437	# ONLY when the local ref does not already exist.
438	#
439	# WHY: `_hydrate_fetch` updates `refs/remotes/origin/<branch>` and deliberately
440	# never touches `refs/heads`. On a CI runner refs/heads therefore never exists —
441	# so `_artifact_persist_snapshot` finds no parent (:229) and ROOTS a new history,
442	# and the `--force` push then orphans everything already on origin. The branch
443	# could never accumulate in CI, the `unchanged` short-circuit could never fire,
444	# and two concurrent runs could clobber each other with no common ancestor.
445	#
446	# ABSENT-ONLY IS THE POINT, not a micro-optimisation. hydrate's manifest states
447	# the invariant: a LOCAL snapshot wins on read when both exist, because it may
448	# carry work an earlier push never delivered. Adopting unconditionally would
449	# discard exactly that work.
450	_artifact_persist_adopt_remote() {
451	    _artifact_persist_reset_status
452	    local issue="${1:-0}" repo_root="${2:-$(git rev-parse --show-toplevel 2>/dev/null)}"
453	
454	    _artifact_persist_has_identity "$issue" || {
455	        _ARTIFACT_PERSIST_LAST_STATUS="empty"
456	        _ARTIFACT_PERSIST_LAST_REASON="no identity to adopt under"
457	        return 0
458	    }
459	
460	    local _gd=""
461	    [[ -n "$repo_root" ]] && _artifact_persist_git_dir_v _gd "$repo_root"
462	    if [[ -z "$repo_root" || ! -d "$_gd" ]]; then
463	        _ARTIFACT_PERSIST_LAST_STATUS="failed"
464	        _ARTIFACT_PERSIST_LAST_REASON="unresolvable repo: repo_root=[${repo_root:-<empty>}] git_dir=[${_gd:-<empty>}]"
465	        return 1
466	    fi
467	
468	    local branch; _artifact_persist_branch_v branch "$issue"
469	
470	    if GIT_DIR="$_gd" git rev-parse -q --verify "refs/heads/$branch" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
471	        _ARTIFACT_PERSIST_LAST_STATUS="kept"
472	        _ARTIFACT_PERSIST_LAST_REASON="local $branch already exists — left untouched"
473	        return 0
474	    fi
475	
476	    local remote_tip
477	    if ! remote_tip="$(GIT_DIR="$_gd" git rev-parse -q --verify "refs/remotes/origin/$branch" 2>/dev/null)" \
478	            || [[ -z "$remote_tip" ]]; then
479	        _ARTIFACT_PERSIST_LAST_STATUS="empty"
480	        _ARTIFACT_PERSIST_LAST_REASON="no refs/remotes/origin/$branch to adopt (first run)"
481	        return 0
482	    fi
483	
484	    local _ar_err; _ar_err="$(mktemp -u "$(zbuild_engine_tmpdir)/zbuild-adopt-err.XXXXXX" 2>/dev/null)" || _ar_err="/dev/null"
485	    [[ -n "$_ar_err" ]] || _ar_err="/dev/null"
486	    if ! GIT_DIR="$_gd" git update-ref "refs/heads/$branch" "$remote_tip" 2>"$_ar_err"; then
487	        local err; err="$(cat "$_ar_err" 2>/dev/null | tr '\n' ' ')"
488	        [[ "$_ar_err" != "/dev/null" ]] && rm -f "$_ar_err"
489	        _ARTIFACT_PERSIST_LAST_STATUS="failed"
490	        _ARTIFACT_PERSIST_LAST_REASON="git update-ref $branch failed: ${err:-<no stderr>} (git_dir=$_gd)"
491	        return 1
492	    fi
493	    [[ "$_ar_err" != "/dev/null" ]] && rm -f "$_ar_err"
494	    _ARTIFACT_PERSIST_LAST_STATUS="adopted"
495	    _ARTIFACT_PERSIST_LAST_REASON="adopted origin/$branch as the local snapshot parent"
496	    return 0
497	}
498	
499	# ─── _artifact_persist_push <issue> [repo_root] (#1071) ─────────────────────
500	# Push `zbuild/state/issue-<N>` to origin.
501	#
502	# WHY THIS DID NOT EXIST: this file has never contained a `git push`. It writes
503	# a LOCAL ref with plumbing and reads `refs/remotes/origin/<branch>` only as a
504	# restore fallback. The only state-branch push in the repository is a shell
505	# block inside `.github/workflows/zbuild-pipeline.yml`, which no local run
506	# executes — so ADR-050 §4's "push the state branch once at the end, pass or
507	# fail" was true of CI and of nothing else. #1921 measured the consequence.
508	#
509	# BEST-EFFORT BY CONTRACT. A failed push degrades to "state is local only",
510	# which is today's behaviour for every local run — so the fallback is already
511	# proven in production. It sets status/reason for the caller to REPORT; a silent
512	# failure here is precisely how #1921 went unnoticed for the life of the
513	# feature.
514	#
515	# `--force` matches the existing CI push: the state branch is a snapshot, not a
516	# history, and a snapshot that refuses to advance because it is not a
517	# fast-forward is a snapshot nobody can use. The concurrency hazard that creates
518	# is #1764's, and it is answered by ADR-059 §4's per-issue admission lock — not
519	# by making this a non-force push, which would simply fail instead.
520	_artifact_persist_push() {
521	    _artifact_persist_reset_status
522	    local issue="${1:-0}" repo_root="${2:-$(git rev-parse --show-toplevel 2>/dev/null)}"
523	    _artifact_persist_has_identity "$issue" || {
524	        _ARTIFACT_PERSIST_LAST_STATUS="empty"
525	        _ARTIFACT_PERSIST_LAST_REASON="no identity to push under (issue=${issue:-<empty>}, no goal)"
526	        return 0
527	    }
528	    local _gd=""
529	    [[ -n "$repo_root" ]] && _artifact_persist_git_dir_v _gd "$repo_root"
530	    if [[ -z "$repo_root" || ! -d "$_gd" ]]; then
531	        _ARTIFACT_PERSIST_LAST_STATUS="failed"
532	        _ARTIFACT_PERSIST_LAST_REASON="unresolvable repo: repo_root=[${repo_root:-<empty>}] git_dir=[${_gd:-<empty>}]"
533	        return 1
534	    fi
535	
536	    local branch; _artifact_persist_branch_v branch "$issue"
537	    if ! GIT_DIR="$_gd" git rev-parse -q --verify "refs/heads/$branch" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
538	        _ARTIFACT_PERSIST_LAST_STATUS="empty"
539	        _ARTIFACT_PERSIST_LAST_REASON="no local branch $branch to push (nothing was snapshotted)"
540	        return 0
541	    fi
542	    if ! GIT_DIR="$_gd" git remote get-url origin >/dev/null 2>&1; then
543	        _ARTIFACT_PERSIST_LAST_STATUS="empty"
544	        _ARTIFACT_PERSIST_LAST_REASON="no origin remote configured"
545	        return 0
546	    fi
547	
548	    local _p_err; _p_err="$(mktemp "$(zbuild_engine_tmpdir)/zbuild-push-err.XXXXXX" 2>/dev/null || printf '')"
549	    if GIT_DIR="$_gd" git push --force origin \
550	            "refs/heads/$branch:refs/heads/$branch" 2>"${_p_err:-/dev/null}"; then
551	        _ARTIFACT_PERSIST_LAST_STATUS="saved"
552	        _ARTIFACT_PERSIST_LAST_REASON="pushed $branch to origin"
553	        [[ -n "$_p_err" ]] && rm -f "$_p_err"
554	        return 0
555	    fi
556	    local err=""; [[ -n "$_p_err" ]] && err="$(tr '\n' ' ' 2>/dev/null < "$_p_err" | cut -c1-300)"
557	    [[ -n "$_p_err" ]] && rm -f "$_p_err"
558	    _ARTIFACT_PERSIST_LAST_STATUS="failed"
559	    _ARTIFACT_PERSIST_LAST_REASON="git push $branch failed: ${err:-<no stderr>}"
560	    return 1
561	}
562	
563	# ─── _artifact_persist_restore <issue> <restored_dir> [repo_root] ───────────
564	# Extract the tip of the state branch into <restored_dir> (created if absent).
565	# Prefers a local refs/heads/<branch>; falls back to refs/remotes/origin/<branch>
566	# when only the fetched remote ref is present (CI). No-op (rc 0, empty dir) when
567	# no state branch exists. Never touches the working tree.
568	_artifact_persist_restore() {
569	    _artifact_persist_reset_status
570	    local issue="${1:-0}" restored_dir="$2" repo_root="${3:-$(git rev-parse --show-toplevel 2>/dev/null)}"
571	    # Resolve the SHARED git dir (see _artifact_persist_git_dir). Two reasons:
572	    #   1. refs must be read from the shared store, not a per-worktree view;
573	    #   2. the old guard tested `-d "$repo_root/.git"`, which is FALSE in a linked
574	    #      worktree because .git is a file there — restore would silently no-op and
575	    #      prior artifacts would never come back, with no error to notice.
576	    local _gd=""
577	    [[ -n "$repo_root" ]] && _artifact_persist_git_dir_v _gd "$repo_root"
578	    [[ -z "$restored_dir" ]] && { _ARTIFACT_PERSIST_LAST_STATUS="failed"
579	        _ARTIFACT_PERSIST_LAST_REASON="no restored_dir given"; return 2; }
580	    if [[ -z "$repo_root" || ! -d "$_gd" ]]; then
581	        _ARTIFACT_PERSIST_LAST_STATUS="failed"
582	        _ARTIFACT_PERSIST_LAST_REASON="unresolvable repo: repo_root=[${repo_root:-<empty>}] git_dir=[${_gd:-<empty>}] cwd=[$PWD]"
583	        return 1
584	    fi
585	
586	    local branch; _artifact_persist_branch_v branch "$issue"
587	    local ref=""
588	    if GIT_DIR="$_gd" git rev-parse -q --verify "refs/heads/$branch" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
589	        ref="refs/heads/$branch"
590	        _ARTIFACT_PERSIST_LAST_SOURCE="local"
591	    elif GIT_DIR="$_gd" git rev-parse -q --verify "refs/remotes/origin/$branch" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
592	        ref="refs/remotes/origin/$branch"
593	        _ARTIFACT_PERSIST_LAST_SOURCE="remote"
594	    else
595	        # A first-ever run for this issue. Genuinely nothing to restore — the one
596	        # early return here that is NOT a failure.
597	        _ARTIFACT_PERSIST_LAST_STATUS="empty"
598	        _ARTIFACT_PERSIST_LAST_REASON="no $branch locally or on origin (first run)"
599	        return 0
600	    fi
601	
602	    if ! mkdir -p "$restored_dir"; then
603	        _ARTIFACT_PERSIST_LAST_STATUS="failed"
604	        _ARTIFACT_PERSIST_LAST_REASON="mkdir -p $restored_dir failed"
605	        return 1
606	    fi
607	    # git archive streams the tree; tar unpacks it, no checkout / index change.
608	    # #1878: PIPESTATUS, not the pipeline rc — a failing `git archive` piped into
609	    # a happy `tar` yields rc=0, so a broken restore reported success.
610	    # PR #1880 review: guarded (see the _ct_err note above).
611	    local _ar_err; _ar_err="$(mktemp -u "$(zbuild_engine_tmpdir)/zbuild-restore-err.XXXXXX" 2>/dev/null)" || _ar_err="/dev/null"
612	    [[ -n "$_ar_err" ]] || _ar_err="/dev/null"
613	    GIT_DIR="$_gd" git archive "$ref" 2>"$_ar_err" | tar -x -C "$restored_dir" 2>>"$_ar_err"
614	    local _st=("${PIPESTATUS[@]}")
615	    if [[ "${_st[0]}" -ne 0 || "${_st[1]}" -ne 0 ]]; then
616	        local err; err="$(cat "$_ar_err" 2>/dev/null | tr '\n' ' ')"
617	        rm -f "$_ar_err"
618	        _ARTIFACT_PERSIST_LAST_STATUS="failed"
619	        _ARTIFACT_PERSIST_LAST_REASON="restore of $ref failed (archive rc=${_st[0]} tar rc=${_st[1]}): ${err:-<no stderr>}"
620	        return 1
621	    fi
622	    rm -f "$_ar_err"
623	    # PR #1880 review: "restored", NOT "saved". The same channel carries both
624	    # operations' outcomes, so reusing "saved" would let a caller checking
625	    # `== "saved"` to confirm a SNAPSHOT be satisfied by a restore that happened
626	    # to run first — the restore runs once at startup, before any snapshot.
627	    _ARTIFACT_PERSIST_LAST_STATUS="restored"
628	    _ARTIFACT_PERSIST_LAST_REASON="restored from $ref"
629	    return 0
630	}
631	
632	# ─── _artifact_persist_put_back <from> <to> (#1805, ADR-006 §3.6) ───────────
633	# Copy every file under <from> to the same place under <to>, skipping any file
634	# <to> already has (no-clobber). stage-io/ records are excluded (one run's
635	# model calls, not stage output). Identical semantics to _hydrate_put_back;
636	# extracted here so the runner's resume rehydration and the hydrate plugin
637	# share one implementation.
638	_artifact_persist_put_back() {
639	    local from="$1" to="$2" f rel
640	    mkdir -p "$to" || return 1
641	    while IFS= read -r -d '' f; do
642	        rel="${f#"$from"/}"
643	        # Guard: skip if strip failed (trailing slash on $from) — rel would be absolute.
644	        # Also skip dotdot traversal components (../../etc/passwd style, foo/..) which
645	        # the absolute-path check does not catch.
646	        [[ "$rel" == /* || "$rel" == *../* || "$rel" == ..* || "$rel" == *.. ]] && continue
647	        [[ "$rel" == stage-io/* || -e "$to/$rel" ]] && continue
648	        mkdir -p "$(dirname "$to/$rel")" && cp -p "$f" "$to/$rel" || return 1
649	    done < <(find "$from" -type f -print0 2>/dev/null)
650	    return 0
651	}

193	assert_eq \
194	    "[#1805/DSITER-1] without _ZBUILD_RESUME_ACTIVE, fresh run starts at iter=1 (guard prevents iter-skip)" \
195	    "1" "$_SPEC7_FRESH_FIRST_ITER"
196	
197	# ── [#1805/DSITER-1] write side: current_iter persisted before first dispatch ─────
198	# The read-side tests above pre-seed current_iter=2 and verify the orchestrator
199	# READS it. This sub-case verifies the WRITE side: at the moment
200	# cycle_dispatch_stage is first called for iter=1 on a fresh run, current_iter=1
201	# must already be in the state file (written by _cycle_state_write_iter_start).
202	# Without _cycle_state_write_iter_start the value would remain at its init value
203	# (0 / absent) at dispatch time and this assertion would FAIL.
204	print_test_section "[#1805/DSITER-1] write side: current_iter=1 persisted in state before first cycle_dispatch_stage call"
205	
206	# Given — a fresh run (no resume); state file has no prior cycle iterations;
207	#   _ZBUILD_RESUME_ACTIVE is unset so this exercises the fresh-run write path.
208	: > "$ZBUILD_EVENTS_JSONL"
209	jq -n '{schema_version:1, stage_statuses:{}, updated_at:"seed"}' > "$STATE_FILE"
210	load_template "$FIXT/cycle-converges-iter2.yaml"
211	unset _ZBUILD_RESUME_ACTIVE
212	
213	# When the orchestrator runs, capture current_iter from the state file at the
214	# moment cycle_dispatch_stage is first called. This pins write-before-dispatch.
215	_SPEC7W_CURRENT_ITER_AT_FIRST_DISPATCH=-99
216	_SPEC7W_FIRST_DISPATCH_SEEN=0
217	cycle_dispatch_stage() {
218	    local stage="$1" iter="$2"
219	    if [[ "$_SPEC7W_FIRST_DISPATCH_SEEN" -eq 0 ]]; then
220	        _SPEC7W_FIRST_DISPATCH_SEEN=1
221	        _SPEC7W_CURRENT_ITER_AT_FIRST_DISPATCH="$(jq -r \
222	            '.cycle_iterations["build-test"].current_iter // -99' \
223	            "$STATE_FILE" 2>/dev/null || echo "-99")"
224	    fi
225	    _CYCLE_DISPATCH_VERDICT="pass"
226	    _CYCLE_DISPATCH_STATUS="complete"
227	    return 0
228	}
229	
230	zb_stub_reports_tests test
231	
232	# When — cycle orchestrator runs a fresh iteration 1 (no resume).
233	set +e
234	cycle_orchestrator_run "build-test" "$ZBUILD_STATE_DIR" "$STATE_FILE"
235	_s7w_rc=$?
236	set -e
237	
238	# Then — at the moment cycle_dispatch_stage was first called for iter=1,
239	# current_iter in the state file was already 1.
240	# If _cycle_state_write_iter_start is removed: current_iter stays at init value
241	# (0 → or absent → -99 fallback) → assert "1" == "0" or "1" == "-99" → FAILS.
242	# After the change: _cycle_state_write_iter_start writes current_iter=1 before
243	# cycle_dispatch_stage is called → assert "1" == "1" → PASSES.
244	assert_eq \
245	    "[#1805/DSITER-1] current_iter=1 written to state before first cycle_dispatch_stage call (write-before-dispatch; removing _cycle_state_write_iter_start leaves current_iter at init value)" \
246	    "1" "$_SPEC7W_CURRENT_ITER_AT_FIRST_DISPATCH"
247	
248	# ── [#1805/DSCMBR-1] cycle member stages already complete in iter k are skipped ─
249	# On resume, within the interrupted iteration, cycle member stages already marked
250	# complete in persisted state are skipped; the first dispatched cycle member is
251	# the interrupted stage.
252	print_test_section "[#1805/DSCMBR-1] complete cycle members in interrupted iter skipped; interrupted member dispatched"
253	
254	# Given — a run is being resumed; in the interrupted iteration (iter 2), member
255	#   stage "build" completed and member stage "test" was interrupted before
256	#   completing; persisted state records build as complete within iter 2.
257	#   _ZBUILD_RESUME_ACTIVE=true is exported.
258	: > "$ZBUILD_EVENTS_JSONL"
259	jq -n '{schema_version:1, stage_statuses:{}, updated_at:"seed"}' > "$STATE_FILE"
260	
261	# Use zb_engine_loop_state to write cycle state: 2 rounds (iter 1 finished,
262	# iter 2 in_progress = current interrupted iter). After this call,
263	# cycle_iterations["build-test"].current_iter = 2.
264	zb_engine_loop_state "$STATE_FILE" "build-test" 2 5 "in_progress"
265	
266	# Record that "build" completed in iter 2 before the interruption, and that
267	# "test" was interrupted (and therefore "aborted" — the value
268	# _cycle_state_write_member_atomic writes for an interrupted/aborted stage).
269	# Using "aborted" here (not "in_progress", which is never written by the real code)
270	# ensures the skip-guard check (`stage_statuses[$s] == "complete"`) is exercised on
271	# the production data shape: build=complete → skipped; test=aborted → dispatched.
272	# stage_statuses is what the cycle orchestrator checks to decide whether to skip a
273	# member on resume (ADR-006 §3.6 / DSCMBR-1).
274	# Use jq to merge this into the existing state; the cycle_iterations block
275	# written by zb_engine_loop_state is preserved (`.` merge keeps all other fields).
276	jq '.stage_statuses.build = "complete" | .stage_statuses.test = "aborted"' "$STATE_FILE" \
277	    > "${STATE_FILE}.cmbr1.tmp" && mv "${STATE_FILE}.cmbr1.tmp" "$STATE_FILE"
278	
279	# Load the template: cycle-converges-iter2.yaml has build + test as cycle members,
280	# matching the state above.
281	load_template "$FIXT/cycle-converges-iter2.yaml"
282	
283	# Track which cycle members are dispatched. cycle_dispatch_stage is what causes
284	# stage.start events in a unit-test context; not being called for "build" is
285	# functionally equivalent to no stage.start for build.
286	_CMBR1_BUILD_DISPATCHED=0
287	_CMBR1_TEST_DISPATCHED=0
288	cycle_dispatch_stage() {
289	    local stage="$1" iter="$2"
290	    if [[ "$stage" == "build" ]]; then
291	        _CMBR1_BUILD_DISPATCHED=1
292	    elif [[ "$stage" == "test" ]]; then
293	        _CMBR1_TEST_DISPATCHED=1
294	    fi
295	    _CYCLE_DISPATCH_VERDICT="pass"
296	    _CYCLE_DISPATCH_STATUS="complete"
297	    return 0
298	}
299	
300	zb_stub_reports_tests test
301	
302	# When — _ZBUILD_RESUME_ACTIVE=true is exported and the cycle orchestrator
303	#   dispatches members of iter k (iter 2). "build" is complete; "test" is pending.
304	set +e
305	export _ZBUILD_RESUME_ACTIVE=true
306	cycle_orchestrator_run "build-test" "$ZBUILD_STATE_DIR" "$STATE_FILE"
307	_cmbr1_rc=$?
308	set -e
309	
310	# Then — no stage.start event for "build" (already complete in iter k):
311	# cycle_dispatch_stage must NOT be called for "build" in iter 2.
312	# Before the change: orchestrator does not check member state on resume →
313	#   dispatches build regardless → _CMBR1_BUILD_DISPATCHED=1 → assert 0==1 → FAILS.
314	# After the change: orchestrator sees stage_statuses.build=complete in iter 2 →
315	#   skips build → _CMBR1_BUILD_DISPATCHED=0 → PASSES.
316	assert_eq \
317	    "[#1805/DSCMBR-1] no stage.start for 'build' in iter 2 (complete member skipped on resume within interrupted iter)" \
318	    "0" "$_CMBR1_BUILD_DISPATCHED"
319	
320	# Then — stage.start is emitted for "test" (the interrupted member of iter k):
321	# cycle_dispatch_stage must be called for "test" in iter 2.
322	# Before the change: if orchestrator skips ALL members or aborts, test never
323	#   dispatches → _CMBR1_TEST_DISPATCHED=0 → assert 1==0 → FAILS.
324	# After the change: orchestrator skips build, dispatches test →
325	#   _CMBR1_TEST_DISPATCHED=1 → PASSES.
326	assert_eq \
327	    "[#1805/DSCMBR-1] stage.start emitted for 'test' in iter 2 (interrupted cycle member dispatched on resume)" \
328	    "1" "$_CMBR1_TEST_DISPATCHED"
329	
330	# ── [#1805/DSCMBR-1] iter=1 scenario: most common interruption point ────────────
331	# Red-team finding: DSCMBR-1 skip guard must work for any interrupted iteration,
332	# including iter=1 (the most common first-failure point). The guard must NOT
333	# require _start_iter > 1; if it does, complete iter-1 members are re-dispatched.
334	print_test_section "[#1805/DSCMBR-1] iter=1 interrupted: build complete in iter=1 is skipped, test dispatched"
335	
336	# Given — a run is being resumed; in the interrupted iteration (iter 1), member
337	#   stage "build" completed and member stage "test" was interrupted before
338	#   completing; persisted state records build as complete within iter 1.
339	#   _ZBUILD_RESUME_ACTIVE=true is exported.
340	: > "$ZBUILD_EVENTS_JSONL"
341	jq -n '{schema_version:1, stage_statuses:{}, updated_at:"seed"}' > "$STATE_FILE"
342	
343	# Use zb_engine_loop_state to write cycle state: 1 round → current_iter=1
344	# (interrupted during iter 1; this is the most common interruption scenario).
345	# cycle_iterations["build-test"].current_iter = 1 (_start_iter = 1 on resume).
346	zb_engine_loop_state "$STATE_FILE" "build-test" 1 5 "in_progress"
347	
348	# Record that "build" completed in iter 1 before the interruption.
349	# stage_statuses.build = "complete" is what the cycle orchestrator checks to
350	# decide whether to skip a member on resume (ADR-006 §3.6 / DSCMBR-1).
351	jq '.stage_statuses.build = "complete"' "$STATE_FILE" \
352	    > "${STATE_FILE}.cmbr1i1.tmp" && mv "${STATE_FILE}.cmbr1i1.tmp" "$STATE_FILE"
353	
354	# Load the template: same cycle-converges-iter2.yaml, build + test as cycle members.
355	load_template "$FIXT/cycle-converges-iter2.yaml"
356	
357	# Track which cycle members are dispatched. cycle_dispatch_stage causes stage.start
358	# events in a unit-test context; not being called for "build" is functionally
359	# equivalent to no stage.start for build.
360	_CMBR1I1_BUILD_DISPATCHED=0
361	_CMBR1I1_TEST_DISPATCHED=0
362	cycle_dispatch_stage() {
363	    local stage="$1" iter="$2"
364	    if [[ "$stage" == "build" ]]; then
365	        _CMBR1I1_BUILD_DISPATCHED=1
366	    elif [[ "$stage" == "test" ]]; then
367	        _CMBR1I1_TEST_DISPATCHED=1
368	    fi
369	    _CYCLE_DISPATCH_VERDICT="pass"
370	    _CYCLE_DISPATCH_STATUS="complete"
371	    return 0
372	}
373	
374	zb_stub_reports_tests test
375	
376	# When — _ZBUILD_RESUME_ACTIVE=true is exported and the cycle orchestrator
377	#   dispatches members of iter 1. "build" is complete; "test" is pending.
378	set +e
379	export _ZBUILD_RESUME_ACTIVE=true
380	cycle_orchestrator_run "build-test" "$ZBUILD_STATE_DIR" "$STATE_FILE"
381	_cmbr1i1_rc=$?
382	set -e
383	
384	# Then — no stage.start event for "build" (already complete in iter 1).
385	# cycle_dispatch_stage must NOT be called for "build" in iter 1.
386	# Before the fix: DSCMBR-1 guard requires _start_iter > 1; for _start_iter=1 the
387	#   condition is false, _cid_resume_first_iter stays false → build IS dispatched →
388	#   _CMBR1I1_BUILD_DISPATCHED=1 → assert 0==1 → FAILS (exposes the code bug).
389	# After the fix: guard works for _start_iter=1 too → build is skipped →
390	#   _CMBR1I1_BUILD_DISPATCHED=0 → PASSES.
391	assert_eq \
392	    "[#1805/DSCMBR-1] no stage.start for 'build' in iter 1 (complete member skipped on resume within interrupted iter=1; DSCMBR-1 guard must work for _start_iter=1 not only _start_iter>1)" \
393	    "0" "$_CMBR1I1_BUILD_DISPATCHED"
394	
395	# Then — stage.start is emitted for "test" (the interrupted member of iter 1).
396	# cycle_dispatch_stage must be called for "test" in iter 1.
397	# Before the fix: build is re-dispatched and test may also run, but the guard
398	#   failure means the skip invariant is violated.
399	# After the fix: build is skipped, test is dispatched →
400	#   _CMBR1I1_TEST_DISPATCHED=1 → PASSES.
401	assert_eq \
402	    "[#1805/DSCMBR-1] stage.start emitted for 'test' in iter 1 (interrupted cycle member dispatched; DSCMBR-1 applies to iter=1 not only iter>1)" \
403	    "1" "$_CMBR1I1_TEST_DISPATCHED"
404	
405	# ── DSCYCL-1: test uses a fixture containing a cyclic stage ────────────────────
406	print_test_section "resume-loop-state test uses a fixture containing a cyclic stage"
407	
408	# cycle-converges-iter2.yaml is loaded above via load_template and driven through
409	# cycle_orchestrator_run. Assert it contains type: cycle to formally pin the fixture
410	# contains a cyclic stage (as DSCYCL-1 requires).
411	# Then — the fixture used by this test file contains a stage of type: cycle
412	_s13_loop_fixt_content="$(cat "$FIXT/cycle-converges-iter2.yaml")"
413	assert_contains "[#1805/DSCYCL-1] cycle fixture used by resume-loop-state test has type: cycle" \
414	    "$_s13_loop_fixt_content" "type: cycle"
415	
416	# Also assert the pipeline was actually run: cycle_dispatch_stage was invoked
417	# during cycle_orchestrator_run above, setting _SPEC7_FIRST_ITER from its
418	# initial -1. A value > -1 proves the cyclic stage was dispatched.
419	assert_gt \
420	    "resume-loop-state ran the cyclic pipeline (cycle_dispatch_stage was invoked)" \
421	    "$_SPEC7_FIRST_ITER" "-1"
422	
423	cleanup_test_env
424	print_test_results
425	exit $((FAIL > 0))

1	#!/usr/bin/env bash
2	# Tests: pipeline resume CLI + auto-resume policy (issue #225)
3	# Covers:
4	#   (a) get_resume_recommendation returns auto_resume for in_progress state < 24h
5	#   (b) returns fresh_start for complete
6	#   (c) returns manual_resume_only for aborted
7	#   (d) pipeline resume with staged state skips completed stages
8	#   (e) --force overrides aborted status
9	set -euo pipefail
10	
11	SCRIPT_DIR="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)"
12	REPO_ROOT="$(cd "$SCRIPT_DIR/../.." && pwd)"
13	
14	# shellcheck source=../scripts/lib/helpers.sh
15	source "$REPO_ROOT/scripts/lib/helpers.sh"
16	# shellcheck source=../lib/test-helpers.sh
17	source "$REPO_ROOT/tests/lib/test-helpers.sh"
18	# shellcheck source=../core/state/resume.sh
19	source "$REPO_ROOT/core/state/resume.sh"
20	
21	print_test_header "pipeline resume — CLI + auto-resume policy (#225)"
22	
23	setup_test_env "pipeline-resume"
24	
25	# #1921 follow-up: reserved test identity (zb_test_issue). These were real
26	# issue numbers; a run keyed to one writes fabricated prior work onto that
27	# issue's state branch. Only identity positions and the strings DERIVED from
28	# them are swept — a bare number elsewhere is not an identity.
29	_ZB_ID="$(zb_test_issue)"
30	# Wave 12-E (#664): default is enforce. Stub plugins used here lack honest
31	# inputs/outputs blocks; opt out — this suite tests resume policy.
32	export ZBUILD_CONTRACT_VALIDATOR=warn
33	STATE_FILE="$TEST_TEMP_DIR/state/pipeline-state.json"
34	mkdir -p "$(dirname "$STATE_FILE")"
35	
36	# ── Helper: write a minimal state file ───────────────────────────────────────
37	# Usage: _write_state <status> [updated_at] [stage_statuses_json]
38	_write_state() {
39	    local status="$1"
40	    local updated_at="${2:-$(date -u +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ)}"
41	    local stage_statuses_json="${3:-{\}}"
42	    # Build JSON without passing stage_statuses as argjson to avoid shell quoting issues
43	    jq -n \
44	        --arg status "$status" \
45	        --arg updated_at "$updated_at" \
46	        --argjson _ZB_ID "$_ZB_ID" \
47	        '{
48	            schema_version: 1,
49	            run_id: "test-run-225",
50	            issue: $_ZB_ID,
51	            stage_statuses: {},
52	            current_iteration: 0,
53	            self_heal_count: {},
54	            scope_manifest_hash: "",
55	            cost_ledger_pointer: 0,
56	            claim_lease_id: "",
57	            plugin_state: {},
58	            status: $status,
59	            updated_at: $updated_at
60	        }' > "$STATE_FILE"
61	    # Merge stage_statuses separately if provided
62	    if [[ "$stage_statuses_json" != "{}" && "$stage_statuses_json" != '{\}' ]]; then
63	        local tmp; tmp="$(mktemp)"
64	        jq --argjson ss "$stage_statuses_json" '.stage_statuses = $ss' "$STATE_FILE" > "$tmp"
65	        mv "$tmp" "$STATE_FILE"
66	    fi
67	}
68	
69	# ─── (a) auto_resume for in_progress < 24h ──────────────────────────────────
70	print_test_section "get_resume_recommendation: in_progress < 24h"
71	
72	_write_state "in_progress" "$(date -u +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ)"
73	result="$(get_resume_recommendation "$STATE_FILE")"
74	assert_eq "in_progress recent → auto_resume" "auto_resume" "$result"
75	
76	# ─── (b) fresh_start for complete ───────────────────────────────────────────
77	print_test_section "get_resume_recommendation: complete"
78	
79	_write_state "complete"
80	result="$(get_resume_recommendation "$STATE_FILE")"
81	assert_eq "complete → fresh_start" "fresh_start" "$result"
82	
83	# ─── (c) manual_resume_only for aborted ─────────────────────────────────────
84	print_test_section "get_resume_recommendation: aborted"
85	
86	_write_state "aborted"
87	result="$(get_resume_recommendation "$STATE_FILE")"
88	assert_eq "aborted → manual_resume_only" "manual_resume_only" "$result"
89	
90	# ─── (b2) fresh_start when no state file ────────────────────────────────────
91	print_test_section "get_resume_recommendation: no state file"
92	
93	rm -f "$STATE_FILE"
94	result="$(get_resume_recommendation "$STATE_FILE")"
95	assert_eq "no state file → fresh_start" "fresh_start" "$result"
96	
97	# ─── (a2) manual_resume_only for in_progress > 24h ──────────────────────────
98	print_test_section "get_resume_recommendation: in_progress > 24h"
99	
100	old_ts="2020-01-01T00:00:00Z"
101	_write_state "in_progress" "$old_ts"
102	result="$(get_resume_recommendation "$STATE_FILE")"
103	assert_eq "in_progress old → manual_resume_only" "manual_resume_only" "$result"
104	
105	# ─── interrupted → auto_resume ──────────────────────────────────────────────
106	print_test_section "get_resume_recommendation: interrupted"
107	
108	_write_state "interrupted"
109	result="$(get_resume_recommendation "$STATE_FILE")"
110	assert_eq "interrupted → auto_resume" "auto_resume" "$result"
111	
112	# ─── (d) pipeline resume skips completed stages ──────────────────────────────
113	print_test_section "runner --resume skips completed stages"
114	
115	# Write a state where 'intake' is complete and 'output' is not
116	_write_state "in_progress" "$(date -u +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ)" \
117	    '{"intake": "complete", "output": "pending"}'
118	
119	# Check that get_state_field reads stage_statuses correctly
120	intake_status="$(get_state_field "$STATE_FILE" '.stage_statuses["intake"]' '')"
121	output_status="$(get_state_field "$STATE_FILE" '.stage_statuses["output"]' '')"
122	assert_eq "intake stage is complete in state" "complete" "$intake_status"
123	assert_eq "output stage is pending in state" "pending" "$output_status"
124	
125	# Simulate the skip logic from the runner: a complete stage should be skipped
126	skipped=false
127	if [[ "$intake_status" == "complete" ]]; then
128	    skipped=true
129	fi
130	assert_eq "completed stage (intake) would be skipped on resume" "true" "$skipped"
131	
132	# ─── (d2) set_pipeline_status via set_state_field ────────────────────────────
133	print_test_section "set_state_field updates pipeline status"
134	
135	_write_state "in_progress"
136	set_state_field "$STATE_FILE" '.status' '"in_progress"'
137	written_status="$(get_state_field "$STATE_FILE" '.status' '')"
138	assert_eq "set_state_field writes status=in_progress" "in_progress" "$written_status"
139	
140	set_state_field "$STATE_FILE" '.status' '"complete"'
141	written_status="$(get_state_field "$STATE_FILE" '.status' '')"
142	assert_eq "set_state_field writes status=complete" "complete" "$written_status"
143	
144	# ─── (e) --force overrides aborted ──────────────────────────────────────────
145	print_test_section "--force: aborted pipeline can be resumed"
146	
147	_write_state "aborted"
148	# Simulate the force override: if force=true, aborted is treated as resumable
149	aborted_status="$(get_state_field "$STATE_FILE" '.status' '')"
150	force=true
151	can_resume=false
152	if [[ "$aborted_status" == "aborted" ]] && $force; then
153	    can_resume=true
154	fi
155	assert_eq "aborted + force=true → can_resume" "true" "$can_resume"
156	
157	# Without force, aborted should not be auto-resumable
158	force=false
159	can_resume=false
160	if [[ "$aborted_status" != "aborted" ]] || $force; then
161	    can_resume=true
162	fi
163	assert_eq "aborted + force=false → cannot auto-resume" "false" "$can_resume"
164	
165	# ─── (e2) get_resume_recommendation still returns manual_resume_only ─────────
166	result="$(get_resume_recommendation "$STATE_FILE")"
167	assert_eq "aborted still returns manual_resume_only (force is caller's responsibility)" \
168	    "manual_resume_only" "$result"
169	
170	# ─── Integration: runner.sh --resume skips completed stages end-to-end ────────
171	print_test_section "integration: runner --resume skips stages with status=complete"
172	
173	# TEMPLATE-AGNOSTIC (#966): resume-skips-completed-stages is a generic runner
174	# behavior, not a property of any shipped roster. Drive a MINIMAL test-owned
175	# fixture (runner-state-dir-minimal.yaml: two leaf stages intake → build)
176	# installed as a per-repo `.zbuild/templates/` overlay (#1270) and run the runner
177	# with CWD = that repo, replacing the retired `--template standard` (#979). The
178	# prior version registered the full 14-stage standard roster and marked 13 stages
179	# complete + one (review) pending; the behavior is stage-count-independent, so we
180	# mark intake=complete + build=pending and re-point the "remaining stage" assertion
181	# from `review` to `build`.
182	RUNNER="$REPO_ROOT/core/pipeline/runner.sh"
183	INT_PLUGINS_ROOT="$TEST_TEMP_DIR/int_plugins"
184	INT_STATE_DIR="$TEST_TEMP_DIR/int_state"
185	INT_EVENTS_DIR="$TEST_TEMP_DIR/int_events"
186	mkdir -p "$INT_PLUGINS_ROOT/agent/intake" "$INT_PLUGINS_ROOT/agent/build" \
187	         "$INT_STATE_DIR" "$INT_EVENTS_DIR"
188	
189	# The fixture's two leaf stages both succeed. #1850/#2366: each declares result
190	# contract 3 and a JSON primary, and writes a contract-3 pass there.
191	for _plugin in intake build; do
192	    _fn="${_plugin//-/_}_run"
193	    cat > "$INT_PLUGINS_ROOT/agent/$_plugin/manifest.yaml" <<EOF
194	id: $_plugin
195	name: Test $_plugin
196	kind: agent
197	version: 0.0.1
198	hooks:
199	  run: ${_fn}
200	requires:
201	  core:
202	    - redaction
203	provides:
204	  result_contract: 3
205	outputs:
206	  - id: ${_fn}_result
207	    path: \${artifact_dir}/${_plugin}-result.json
208	    type: ${_plugin}-result.json@1
209	    format: json
210	    required: true
211	    primary: true
212	    finding_topics: none
213	EOF
214	    cat > "$INT_PLUGINS_ROOT/agent/$_plugin/plugin.sh" <<EOF
215	${_fn}() {
216	    local _art; _art="\${ZBUILD_ARTIFACT_DIR:-\$(dirname "\$2")/artifacts}"
217	    mkdir -p "\$_art"
218	    printf '{"result_contract":3,"outcome":"pass","reason":"stub"}' \\
219	        > "\$_art/${_plugin}-result.json"
220	    return 0
221	}
222	EOF
223	done
224

269	_int_rc=$?
270	set -e
271	
272	assert_eq "integration: --resume exits 0 when remaining stage succeeds" "0" "$_int_rc"
273	assert_file_exists "integration: state file still present after resume" "$INT_STATE_FILE"
274	
275	# Verify the remaining (build) stage status is now complete in state.
276	_build_status="$(jq -r '.stage_statuses.build // empty' "$INT_STATE_FILE" 2>/dev/null)"
277	assert_eq "integration: build stage_status=complete after resume" "complete" "$_build_status"
278	
279	# Verify intake was skipped (events.jsonl should show only 1 stage.start for build).
280	if [[ -f "$INT_EVENTS_DIR/events.jsonl" ]]; then

284	    assert_eq "integration: pipeline.resume event emitted" "1" "$_resume_event"
285	fi
286	
287	# ─── Integration: --from-stage unknown value exits 1 ──────────────────────────
288	# #1850 (ADR-054 §4): a refusal exits 1 (it was 2); the message says which.
289	print_test_section "integration: --from-stage with unknown stage exits 1"
290	
291	set +e
292	( cd "$INT_OVERLAY_REPO" && env \
293	    ZBUILD_CYCLES_ENABLED=0 \
294	    ZBUILD_PLUGINS_ROOT="$INT_PLUGINS_ROOT" \
295	    ZBUILD_STATE_DIR="$INT_STATE_DIR" \
296	    ZBUILD_STATE_FILE="$INT_STATE_FILE" \
297	    ZBUILD_EVENTS_DIR="$INT_EVENTS_DIR" \

302	_fs_rc=$?

304

306	assert_contains "--from-stage unknown stage says it is not a known stage" \

310	print_test_section "integration: --from-stage without --resume exits 1"

314	# fires correctly. Using in_progress would auto-resume instead, changing the

321	      self_heal_count:{},scope_manifest_hash:"",cost_ledger_pointer:0,claim_lease_id:"",
322	      plugin_state:{},status:"complete",updated_at:$now}' > "$INT_STATE_FILE"
323	
324	set +e
325	( cd "$INT_OVERLAY_REPO" && env \
326	    ZBUILD_CYCLES_ENABLED=0 \
327	    ZBUILD_PLUGINS_ROOT="$INT_PLUGINS_ROOT" \
328	    ZBUILD_STATE_DIR="$INT_STATE_DIR" \

1	id: from-stage-combined-resume
2	name: Combined --resume --from-stage test fixture (#1805)
3	extends: simple
4	defaults:
5	  strategy: fanout
6	
7	# Three-stage pipeline for DSFSTG-3: a leaf (intake) before the --from-stage
8	# target, a cycle (cyc) as the target, and a leaf (verify) after the target.
9	# Tests that in combined --resume --from-stage <cyc> mode, stages after <cyc>
10	# (including verify, which may be marked complete in interrupted state) are
11	# still dispatched after the skip_until_stage guard clears at <cyc>.
12	stages:
13	  - id: intake
14	    gate: auto
15	    roles: [intake]
16	  - id: cyc
17	    type: cycle
18	    stages: [cycled]
19	    until:
20	      stage: cycled
21	      field: verdict
22	      op: eq
23	      value: pass
24	    max_iterations: 1
25	    on_max: continue
26	  - id: verify
27	    gate: auto
28	
29	stage_definitions:
30	  cycled:
31	    roles: [builder]

1	#!/usr/bin/env bash
2	# Tests: --from-stage <s> rehydrates completed-stage artifacts before dispatching <s>.
3	# (issue #1805, ADR-006 §3.5 / _runner_from_stage_preflight)
4	#
5	# DSFSTG-1 [code]: --from-stage <s> rehydrates all stages before <s> via
6	#   _artifact_persist_restore and _artifact_persist_put_back, places their
7	#   artifacts in ZBUILD_ARTIFACT_DIR, dispatches <s> as the first stage, and
8	#   emits no stage.start for any earlier stage.
9	#
10	# DSFSTG-2 [code]: --from-stage <s> when a stage before <s> has no restorable
11	#   artifact emits the diagnostic phrase "has no restorable primary artifact"
12	#   to stderr and exits 1 before any stage.start event is emitted.
13	#
14	# DSCYCL-1 [no-code]: the test fixture contains a pipeline stage of type: cycle.
15	set -euo pipefail
16	
17	SCRIPT_DIR="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)"
18	REPO_ROOT="$(cd "$SCRIPT_DIR/../.." && pwd)"
19	RUNNER="$REPO_ROOT/core/pipeline/runner.sh"
20	
21	# shellcheck source=../../scripts/lib/helpers.sh
22	source "$REPO_ROOT/scripts/lib/helpers.sh"
23	# shellcheck source=../../tests/lib/test-helpers.sh
24	source "$REPO_ROOT/tests/lib/test-helpers.sh"
25	# shellcheck source=../../core/state/artifact-persist.sh
26	source "$REPO_ROOT/core/state/artifact-persist.sh"
27	
28	print_test_header "from-stage-rehydrate — artifact restore on --from-stage (#1805)"
29	setup_test_env "from-stage-rehydrate-1805"
30	export ZBUILD_CONTRACT_VALIDATOR=warn
31	
32	# ── SPEC-3: --from-stage rehydrates stages before <s> from git state branch ──
33	print_test_section "[#1805/DSFSTG-1] --from-stage rehydrates stages before <s> and dispatches <s> first"
34	
35	# Given — a previous run completed stages before <s> (intake is complete); their artifacts
36	#   are present in the git state branch; a new invocation uses --from-stage cyc.
37	S3_ID="$(zb_test_issue)"
38	S3_STATE_DIR="$TEST_TEMP_DIR/s3-state"
39	S3_EVENTS_DIR="$TEST_TEMP_DIR/s3-events"
40	S3_EVENTS_JSONL="$S3_EVENTS_DIR/events.jsonl"
41	S3_STATE_FILE="$S3_STATE_DIR/pipeline-state.json"
42	mkdir -p "$S3_STATE_DIR/artifacts" "$S3_EVENTS_DIR"
43	
44	# Create a git repo; _artifact_persist_snapshot writes the state branch here.
45	S3_WORK_REPO="$(setup_git_temp_repo fs-rehydrate-s3)"
46	install_template_overlay "$S3_WORK_REPO" artifact-snapshot-coverage
47	
48	# Create mock plugins (intake + cycled for the artifact-snapshot-coverage cyclic fixture;
49	# cycled is the inner member of the cyc cycle stage, roles:[builder]).
50	mock_plugin_factory "intake" "agent" 0 >/dev/null
51	mock_plugin_factory "build"  "agent" 0 >/dev/null
52	# cycled: inner member of cyc cycle stage (used by SPEC-3 and SPEC-13 sub-case).
53	mock_plugin_factory "cycled" "agent" 0 "" "builder" >/dev/null
54	S3_PLUGINS_ROOT="$TEST_TEMP_DIR/plugins"
55	
56	# Create the intake primary artifact so the snapshot picks it up.
57	printf '{"result_contract":3,"outcome":"pass","reason":"prior-run intake"}' \
58	    > "$S3_STATE_DIR/artifacts/intake-result.json"
59	
60	# Snapshot onto the state branch in S3_WORK_REPO.
61	_s3_snap_rc=0
62	( export ZBUILD_STATE_DIR="$S3_STATE_DIR"
63	  cd "$S3_WORK_REPO" && _artifact_persist_snapshot "$S3_STATE_DIR" "$S3_ID" ) \
64	    >"$TEST_TEMP_DIR/s3-snap.log" 2>&1 || _s3_snap_rc=$?
65	if [[ "$_s3_snap_rc" -ne 0 ]]; then
66	    assert_fail "[#1805/DSFSTG-1] setup: snapshot to state branch failed" \
67	        "rc=$_s3_snap_rc; $(cat "$TEST_TEMP_DIR/s3-snap.log" 2>/dev/null | tail -5)"
68	else
69	    assert_pass "[#1805/DSFSTG-1] setup: state branch populated"
70	fi
71	
72	# Remove the artifact from disk; it now lives only on the state branch.
73	rm -f "$S3_STATE_DIR/artifacts/intake-result.json"
74	
75	# Write state file: intake=complete, cyc=pending, status=in_progress.
76	jq -n \
77	    --arg run_id "s3-fs-1805" \
78	    --arg now "$(date -u +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ)" \
79	    --argjson issue "$S3_ID" \
80	    '{
81	        schema_version: 1,
82	        run_id: $run_id,
83	        issue: $issue,
84	        stage_statuses: {intake: "complete", cyc: "pending"},
85	        current_iteration: 0,
86	        self_heal_count: {},
87	        scope_manifest_hash: "",
88	        cost_ledger_pointer: 0,
89	        claim_lease_id: "",
90	        plugin_state: {},
91	        status: "in_progress",
92	        updated_at: $now
93	    }' > "$S3_STATE_FILE"
94	
95	# Run runner with --from-stage cyc. CWD=S3_WORK_REPO so the state branch
96	# is reachable. Artifact must be restored before cyc (the cycle) dispatches.
97	# When — the runner starts with --from-stage cyc.
98	set +e
99	( cd "$S3_WORK_REPO" && env \
100	    ZBUILD_CYCLES_ENABLED=1 \
101	    ZBUILD_PLUGINS_ROOT="$S3_PLUGINS_ROOT" \
102	    ZBUILD_STATE_DIR="$S3_STATE_DIR" \
103	    ZBUILD_STATE_FILE="$S3_STATE_FILE" \
104	    ZBUILD_EVENTS_DIR="$S3_EVENTS_DIR" \
105	    ZBUILD_EVENTS_JSONL="$S3_EVENTS_JSONL" \
106	    ZBUILD_EVENT_SCHEMA="$REPO_ROOT/config/event-schema.json" \
107	    ZBUILD_CONTRACT_VALIDATOR=warn \
108	    ZBUILD_VISION_GATE=off \
109	    PATH="$PATH" HOME="$HOME" \
110	    bash "$RUNNER" --template artifact-snapshot-coverage \
111	        --resume --from-stage cyc --issue "$S3_ID" ) \
112	    >"$TEST_TEMP_DIR/s3-stdout.txt" 2>"$TEST_TEMP_DIR/s3-stderr.txt"
113	_s3_rc=$?
114	set -e
115	
116	# Then — artifacts from every stage before cyc appear in ZBUILD_ARTIFACT_DIR before
117	# the dispatch loop starts; stage cyc is dispatched as the first stage; no stage.start
118	# for any stage before cyc.
119	
120	# [#1805/DSFSTG-1]: intake artifact must be in ZBUILD_ARTIFACT_DIR after --from-stage.
121	# Before the change: no rehydration → file absent → FAILS.
122	# After the change: _runner_from_stage_preflight restores it → PASSES.
123	assert_file_exists \
124	    "[#1805/DSFSTG-1] intake-result.json rehydrated into ZBUILD_ARTIFACT_DIR via --from-stage" \
125	    "$S3_STATE_DIR/artifacts/intake-result.json"
126	
127	# [#1805/DSFSTG-1]: the restored artifact must carry the payload originally snapshotted to
128	# the git state branch — this proves _artifact_persist_restore read from git and
129	# _artifact_persist_put_back placed it in ZBUILD_ARTIFACT_DIR (not re-created fresh by
130	# the runner through any other mechanism).
131	# Before the change: no restore → file absent → content="" → FAILS.
132	# After the change: git state restore → original content present → PASSES.
133	_s3_restored_content="$(cat "$S3_STATE_DIR/artifacts/intake-result.json" 2>/dev/null || true)"
134	assert_contains \
135	    "[#1805/DSFSTG-1] restored artifact contains original payload (proves _artifact_persist_restore + _artifact_persist_put_back used git state branch)" \
136	    "$_s3_restored_content" "prior-run intake"
137	
138	# [#1805/DSFSTG-1]: pipeline.resume must appear in the events log BEFORE the first
139	# cycle.start event, proving _runner_from_stage_preflight (which calls
140	# _artifact_persist_restore and _artifact_persist_put_back) completed before the
141	# dispatch loop reached stage cyc. pipeline.resume is emitted at the end of the
142	# preflight / rehydration step, before the dispatch loop begins. cycle.start is emitted
143	# when cyc (the --from-stage target) is first dispatched.
144	# Before the change: no preflight → pipeline.resume absent OR no ordering guarantee →
145	#   resume_lineno=0 → assert 0 > 0 → FAILS.
146	# After the change: preflight runs → pipeline.resume emitted → dispatch loop starts →
147	#   cycle.start emitted → resume_lineno < cyc_start_lineno → PASSES.
148	_s3_resume_lineno=0
149	_s3_first_dispatch_lineno=0
150	if [[ -f "$S3_EVENTS_JSONL" ]]; then
151	    _s3_resume_lineno="$(awk '/"pipeline.resume"/{print NR; exit}' "$S3_EVENTS_JSONL" 2>/dev/null)"
152	    _s3_resume_lineno="${_s3_resume_lineno:-0}"
153	    _s3_first_dispatch_lineno="$(awk '/"cycle.start"/{print NR; exit}' "$S3_EVENTS_JSONL" 2>/dev/null)"
154	    _s3_first_dispatch_lineno="${_s3_first_dispatch_lineno:-0}"
155	fi
156	assert_gt "[#1805/DSFSTG-1] pipeline.resume event emitted (from-stage preflight ran before dispatch loop)" \
157	    "$_s3_resume_lineno" "0"
158	assert_gt "[#1805/DSFSTG-1] pipeline.resume precedes first dispatch event (artifact restored before dispatch loop started)" \
159	    "$_s3_first_dispatch_lineno" "$_s3_resume_lineno"
160	
161	# [#1805/DSFSTG-1]: intake must emit no stage.start event (it was skipped).
162	# Before the change: no rehydration means intake might be re-dispatched → stage.start emitted → FAILS.
163	# After the change: intake is complete and skipped entirely → no stage.start → PASSES.
164	_s3_intake_starts=0
165	if [[ -f "$S3_EVENTS_JSONL" ]]; then
166	    _s3_intake_starts="$(jq -r 'select(.type=="stage.start" and .data.stage=="intake") | .type' \
167	        "$S3_EVENTS_JSONL" 2>/dev/null | wc -l | tr -d ' ')"
168	fi
169	assert_eq "[#1805/DSFSTG-1] intake emits no stage.start when skipped via --from-stage" \
170	    "0" "$_s3_intake_starts"
171	
172	# [#1805/DSFSTG-1]: stage <s>=cyc must be dispatched as the first stage and a stage.start
173	# event must be emitted. artifact-snapshot-coverage has intake (leaf) then cyc (cycle).
174	# --from-stage cyc means intake is skipped and cyc is the first thing dispatched.
175	# A cycle stage's inner member (cycled) emits stage.start with stage=cycled when cyc
176	# dispatches it; this is the first stage.start event and proves cyc was dispatched first.
177	# Before the change: without rehydration the runner may re-dispatch intake first →
178	#   stage.start for intake before cycled → no cycled stage.start OR intake dispatched → FAILS.
179	# After the change: intake is skipped; cyc dispatches cycled as first stage → PASSES.
180	_s3_cycled_started=0
181	if [[ -f "$S3_EVENTS_JSONL" ]]; then
182	    _s3_cycled_started="$(jq -r 'select(.type=="stage.start" and .data.stage=="cycled") | .type' \
183	        "$S3_EVENTS_JSONL" 2>/dev/null | wc -l | tr -d ' ')"
184	fi
185	assert_gt "[#1805/DSFSTG-1] stage.start emitted for cycled (inner member of cyc; proves --from-stage target cyc was dispatched as first stage)" \
186	    "$_s3_cycled_started" "0"
187	
188	# [#1805/DSFSTG-1]: pipeline.skip_to_stage must be emitted when --from-stage is active.
189	# RQFROM-2 says the event must be emitted and no earlier stage dispatched after it.
190	# Before the change: no --from-stage support → no pipeline.skip_to_stage event →
191	#   _s3_skip_stage_count=0 → assert 0 > 0 → FAILS.
192	# After the change: runner emits pipeline.skip_to_stage → PASSES.
193	_s3_skip_stage_count=0
194	if [[ -f "$S3_EVENTS_JSONL" ]]; then
195	    _s3_skip_stage_count="$(jq -r 'select(.type=="pipeline.skip_to_stage") | .type' \
196	        "$S3_EVENTS_JSONL" 2>/dev/null | wc -l | tr -d ' ')"
197	fi
198	assert_gt "[#1805/DSFSTG-1] pipeline.skip_to_stage emitted when --from-stage is active (--resume path)" \
199	    "$_s3_skip_stage_count" "0"
200	
201	# [#1805/DSFSTG-1]: no stage before <s>=cyc dispatched after pipeline.skip_to_stage.
202	# intake must not appear as a stage.start event after pipeline.skip_to_stage fires.
203	# Before the change: skip_to_stage absent → lineno=0 → guard skips → intake_after=0
204	#   but skip_stage_count=0 assertion above already fails.
205	# After the change: skip_to_stage fires before dispatch loop; intake is rehydrated
206	#   not dispatched → no stage.start for intake after skip_to_stage → PASSES.
207	_s3_skip_lineno=0
208	_s3_intake_after_skip=0
209	if [[ -f "$S3_EVENTS_JSONL" ]]; then
210	    _s3_skip_lineno="$(awk '/"pipeline.skip_to_stage"/{print NR; exit}' "$S3_EVENTS_JSONL" 2>/dev/null)"
211	    _s3_skip_lineno="${_s3_skip_lineno:-0}"
212	    if [[ "$_s3_skip_lineno" -gt 0 ]]; then
213	        _s3_intake_after_skip="$(awk -v n="$_s3_skip_lineno" \
214	            'NR>n && /"stage\.start"/ && /"intake"/ {c++} END{print c+0}' \
215	            "$S3_EVENTS_JSONL" 2>/dev/null)"
216	    fi
217	fi
218	assert_eq "[#1805/DSFSTG-1] no stage before <s>=cyc dispatched after pipeline.skip_to_stage (--resume path; RQFROM-2)" \
219	    "0" "$_s3_intake_after_skip"
220	
221	# ── SPEC-3b: --from-stage WITHOUT --resume exercises skip_restore=false branch ──
222	# This sub-case covers the plain `--from-stage <s>` path (no --resume flag),
223	# which routes through _runner_from_stage_preflight with skip_restore=false —
224	# the branch that performs the git archive restore itself rather than relying on
225	# a prior resume rehydration step. The existing S3 sub-case always uses
226	# `--resume --from-stage` (skip_restore=true); without this sub-case that
227	# substantively different restore path is never exercised.
228	# (Addresses lens-scope-code finding 1.)
229	print_test_section "[#1805/DSFSTG-1] --from-stage WITHOUT --resume rehydrates stages before <s> (skip_restore=false branch)"
230	
231	# Given — a previous run completed intake; its artifact is present in the git
232	#   state branch; a new invocation uses --from-stage cyc WITHOUT --resume.
233	S5_ID="$(zb_test_issue)"
234	S5_STATE_DIR="$TEST_TEMP_DIR/s5-state"
235	S5_EVENTS_DIR="$TEST_TEMP_DIR/s5-events"
236	S5_EVENTS_JSONL="$S5_EVENTS_DIR/events.jsonl"
237	S5_STATE_FILE="$S5_STATE_DIR/pipeline-state.json"
238	mkdir -p "$S5_STATE_DIR/artifacts" "$S5_EVENTS_DIR"
239	
240	# Fresh git repo; _artifact_persist_snapshot writes the state branch here.
241	S5_WORK_REPO="$(setup_git_temp_repo fs-rehydrate-s5)"
242	install_template_overlay "$S5_WORK_REPO" artifact-snapshot-coverage
243	
244	# Create intake primary artifact so the snapshot picks it up.
245	printf '{"result_contract":3,"outcome":"pass","reason":"prior-run-noresume-intake"}' \
246	    > "$S5_STATE_DIR/artifacts/intake-result.json"
247	
248	# Snapshot onto the state branch in S5_WORK_REPO.
249	_s5_snap_rc=0
250	( export ZBUILD_STATE_DIR="$S5_STATE_DIR"
251	  cd "$S5_WORK_REPO" && _artifact_persist_snapshot "$S5_STATE_DIR" "$S5_ID" ) \
252	    >"$TEST_TEMP_DIR/s5-snap.log" 2>&1 || _s5_snap_rc=$?

647	# Create intake primary artifact so the --from-stage preflight can restore it.
648	printf '{"result_contract":3,"outcome":"pass","reason":"s10-intake-complete"}' \
649	    > "$S10_STATE_DIR/artifacts/intake-result.json"
650	
651	# Snapshot onto the state branch (places intake artifact on git state branch).
652	_s10_snap_rc=0
653	( export ZBUILD_STATE_DIR="$S10_STATE_DIR"
654	  cd "$S10_WORK_REPO" && _artifact_persist_snapshot "$S10_STATE_DIR" "$S10_ID" ) \
655	    >"$TEST_TEMP_DIR/s10-snap.log" 2>&1 || _s10_snap_rc=$?

657	    assert_fail "[#1805/DSFSTG-3] setup s10: snapshot failed" \
